articles.title: Women's Rugby League World Cup: Australia set up fifth straight final vs New Zealand after scare vs debutants Fiji
articles.summary: Defending champions Australia set up a fifth consecutive Women's Rugby League World Cup final against New Zealand after coming from behind to beat a spirited Fiji in Sydney.
articles.body:
Abbi Church scores four tries as Jillaroos come from behind to win 30-14 and reach next weekend's final in Brisbane; Fiji can take plenty of pride from performances in first World Cup; Australia have won last three tournaments; New Zealand blanked Samoa 32-0 in Saturday's first semi-final

Defending champions Australia set up a fifth consecutive Women's Rugby League World Cup final against New Zealand after coming from behind to beat a spirited Fiji in Sydney.

The Jillaroos, who have beaten New Zealand in the last three finals since they were thumped 34-0 by the the Kiwi Ferns in the 2008 showpiece in Brisbane, won 30-14 against Fiji as Abbi Church notched four tries.

Fiji opened up a shock 8-0 lead as Luisa Yaranamua followed a penalty by scoring a try that she also converted, leaving the home side trailing for the first time in the tournament, but Australia made it 8-8 by the break and then dominated the second half.

Australia had won all three of their group games, scoring 242 points and conceding just six, but this was a real test.

Church leapt over the line for the hosts' first try after 25 minutes before Tamika Upton doubled that tally four minutes later to level the scores.

The Jillaroos failed to add the bonus points for both tries, though, as Jocelyn Kelleher missed the conversions.

Fiji ended the first half well, although Australia then took over in the second period as Church scored again prior to a Jaime Chapman try - Kelleher applying the conversions this time.

Church then completed her hat-trick after catching Tarryn Aiken's kick and grounding the ball.

A converted effort from Maria Paseka gave Fiji hope but Church had the final say with her fourth try of the evening - jinking away from two defenders around 30 metres out before sprinting clear to score.

A Fiji team with nowhere near the level of experience of their opponents can be proud of their performance in this game and the tournament as a whole, with the World Cup novices recording group-stage wins over Papua New Guinea and France and pushing New Zealand in an 18-12 defeat in their other match.

New Zealand, aiming to deny Australia a fourth straight World Cup title in Brisbane next Sunday, defeated Samoa 32-0 in Saturday's first semi-final in Newcastle.

articles.title: Latest Heisman Trophy 2026 Odds as CJ Carr Rises, Darian Mensah Falls
articles.summary: The injury that likely ended Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin's regular season may have also impacted wide receiver Jeremiah Smith's Heisman Trophy hopes.
articles.body:
The injury that likely ended Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin's regular season may have also impacted wide receiver Jeremiah Smith's Heisman Trophy hopes.

Smith is no longer the Heisman betting favorite after the Buckeyes lost at USC during their first game without Sayin, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Here's a look at the current Heisman betting odds as Week 10 continues this Saturday.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State: +1900

LaNorris Sellers, QB, South Carolina: +4500

No. 11 Notre Dame's 31-24 upset of No. 1 Miami on Saturday night helped CJ Carr become the new Heisman Trophy betting favorite. He completed 29-of-40 passes for 319 yards and three touchdowns in the win. Miami's Darian Mensah completed 24-of-43 passes for 302 yards, three touchdowns and one interception.

Smith, meanwhile, has struggled to record more than 100 receiving yards per game since Week 5 of Ohio State's season. He connected with true freshman Luke Fahey for 10 catches and 83 yards with a touchdown Halloween night at USC, though he did follow that up with seven catches for 133 yards and a score against Oregon on Saturday.

Smith's drop down the list of betting favorites makes it more likely it will be a quarterback favorited to be honored as the top player in college football this winter.

Utah's Devon Dampier recently improved his betting odds as BYU's Bear Bachmeier's Heisman chances took a hit following No. 3 Utah's 28-20 victory over visiting No. 9 BYU.

Following No. 2 Georgia's 42-7 win over No. 10 Ole Miss on Saturday, Gunner Stockton's odds rose mightily while Trinidad Chambliss' odds fell. Stockton completed 9-of-15 passes for 186 yards and four scores while Chambliss completed 18-of-34 passes for 170 yards and one interception.

Both Tuesday's update of the College Football Playoff selection committee rankings and the next round of Heisman betting odds could look different by the time these key matchups wrap up Saturday night.

articles.title: Lionel Messi wins MLS Golden Boot for second straight year with 26 goals for Inter Miami
articles.summary: Messi also finished with 17 assists, tied for second-most in the league, after another MVP-caliber season.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi once again reigns at the top of MLS, taking home the Golden Boot for the second straight season. Messi finished with 26 goals for Inter Miami, taking the trophy by a notable margin.

FC Dallas' Petar Musa finished in second with 22 goals, followed by 21 goals from Nashville SC's Sam Surridge and 20 goals from the Vancouver Whitecaps' Brian White. However, Messi also finished the season with 17 assists — tied with FC Cincinnati's Evander for the second-highest total in the league.

Messi's final tally came steadily across 31 total games, though the Argentine forward had six multi-goal games, including a four-goal haul in August . Overall, Miami led the league in scoring, with 80 goals scored across the season.

Following a 3-3 draw with Charlotte FC on Saturday's Decision Day, Inter Miami finished second in the Eastern Conference standings, and will enter the postseason as a No. 2 seed. Inter Miami will be defending its title after winning the MLS Cup for the first time last season, starting with a first-round matchup against the Columbus Crew.

Nashville is the No. 1 overall seed for the playoffs after winning the MLS Supporters' Shield with a historic 77 points. Nashville has crushed opponents all season, taking just three losses while allowing a league-low 25 goals.

The Vancouver Whitecaps, who Miami beat to win the 2025 Cup, are the No. 1 seed in the West after continuing their dominance into 2026.

Messi, who has won league MVP in 2024 and 2025, will also see if he can take the title for the third straight year. The forward has a bit more competition this year, with players like White and Surridge having breakout seasons, but the seemingly ageless Messi still feels like a lock for the individual honor.

articles.title: Lionel Messi Wins Historic 2026 MLS Golden Boot Award, Full Stats From Inter Miami Regular Season
articles.summary: Lionel Messi has added more hardware to his collection.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi has added more hardware to his collection.

Messi won the MLS Golden Boot award for the 2026 regular season and became the first player in league history to earn the honor in back-to-back years, per ESPN's Lizzy Becherano .

The Inter Miami star secured the award by racking up a league-high 26 goals in 31 games, including 29 starts. He also recorded 17 assists.

Messi wasn't able to score during Inter Miami's final match of the regular season on Saturday, which ended in a 3-3 draw with Charlotte FC. He picked up one assist in the contest, though.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner is also a strong contender to earn MLS MVP honors for the third consecutive season.

If Messi is able to do so, he'd become the first three-time MVP in MLS history.

His first honor came after he helped Inter Miami win the Supporters' Shield in 2024 before his second occurred once he led his squad to the MLS Cup title in 2025.

Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González recently made the case for Messi to receive MVP recognition.

"I have no doubt that he's the best of all," González said, per Becherano. "None of them can compare to him when it comes to respect for his colleagues.

"Leo at his age and what he does, from my point of view, deserves the MVP and also the Ballon d'Or. I hope he can achieve it."

Messi and Miami are now preparing for the MLS playoffs as the No. 2 seed, as they're set to face the Columbus Crew in best-of-three series to begin the postseason.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin Reacts to LSU's Loss vs. Alabama as Record Drops to 6-3 Ahead of Arch, Texas Matchup
articles.summary: LSU football head coach Lane Kiffin called the No. 14 Tigers' 31-13 home loss to No. 5 Alabama "really disappointing" during his postgame press conference.
articles.body:
LSU football head coach Lane Kiffin called the No. 14 Tigers' 31-13 home loss to No. 5 Alabama "really disappointing" during his postgame press conference .

It's hard to disagree given how well LSU performed outside the scoreboard. The Tigers out-gained Alabama 457-285 and earned more than twice as many first downs (27-13). Quarterback Sam Leavitt threw for 380 yards, one week after amassing 388 vs. Auburn. Alabama's run game also got shut down, with the Crimson Tide rushing for just 79 yards on 29 touches (2.7 YPC).

However, LSU went 0-of-4 on fourth down and couldn't finish drives. Five of LSU's 10 drives went for 53 or more yards, but they resulted in just 13 points (one touchdown, two field goals and two turnovers on downs).

The Tigers also didn't make plays on special teams. Scott Starzyk missed a 56-yard field goal that would have given LSU an early 6-3 lead. Granted, though, that's a long field goal attempt, especially in the college ranks.

However, the biggest issue was allowing a 32-yard punt return from Ryan Coleman-Williams to set Alabama up on the LSU 25-yard line with just under 10 minutes left in the fourth quarter and the Crimson Tide up 17-13. On the next play, 'Bama quarterback Keelon Russell hit wide receiver Cederian Morgan for a 25-yard touchdown and 23-13 lead.

That helped Alabama ultimately score the game's last 21 points in an 18-point win.

It was a bewildering loss for LSU, and Kiffin noted how the passing-game stats should have symbolized a better result.

"I was looking at a sheet and it said Sam [Leavitt] had 380 yards passing and Jackson Harris had 11 [receptions] for 166 [yards] and Trey'Dez [Green] had 10 [receptions] for 85 [yards]. I wouldn't think that would equal 13 points," Kiffin said. "But you got to score touchdowns in the red zone."

Kiffin was also asked why LSU hasn't been able to make winning plays.

"I don't know," he said. "We had a chance."

LSU has now dropped to 6-3 (3-3 SEC) in Kiffin's first season. The Tigers could very well be 8-1 but lost close, down-to-the-wire contests at Ole Miss (32-24) and art Kentucky (35-34 in overtime).

Still, the Tigers' season isn't over yet, and now they have a crucially important matchup with No. 7 Texas, which just beat No. 18 Missouri 34-20 on the road thanks in part to quarterback Arch Manning's 297 passing yards and three touchdowns.

LSU will then close the regular season with road games at No. 13 Tennessee and Arkansas.

articles.title: Deion Sanders, Colorado vs. ASU Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: The Arizona State Sun Devils defeated Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes 20-10 on Saturday in Tempe, Arizona.
articles.body:
The Arizona State Sun Devils defeated Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes 20-10 on Saturday in Tempe, Arizona.

The Sun Devils entered the matchup as 3.5-point favorites over the Buffaloes, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Sanders and the Buffs fell to 3-6 on the season after snapping a five-game losing streak with a 27-24 overtime win over the Kansas State Wildcats last week. It was Colorado's first win since Sept. 12.

The Buffaloes have struggled at quarterback, with junior Isaac Wilson stepping in for sophomore Julian Lewis after the team's third game of the season, a 41-7 blowout loss to Northwestern. That was also the team's first loss of the season.

Wilson struggled Saturday, throwing for 248 yards while throwing one touchdown and one interception.

The Buffs were held scoreless in the first half, with Isaac Wilson completing 8-of-11 pass attempts for just 93 yards. Arizona State's Jake Fette led his team with one touchdown and 101 yards on 77 percent passing to take a 17-0 lead into the break.

Sun Devils running back Cardae Mack also threw a touchdown, completing both of his pass attempts to give Arizona State an advantage.

The Buffaloes flipped the script after halftime, outscoring ASU 10-3 in the second half. However, Colorado could not overcome the deficit after surrendering too many points in the first half as the Sun Devils sealed the 10 point win.

The Buffs will host the Houston Cougars next Friday, with kickoff scheduled for 10:15 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Darian Mensah, CJ Carr's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock as Notre Dame Upsets Miami
articles.summary: Notre Dame shocked the nation Saturday, defeating the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes 31-24 in St. Joseph County, Indiana.
articles.body:
Notre Dame shocked the nation Saturday, defeating the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes 31-24 in St. Joseph County, Indiana.

No. 11-ranked Notre Dame entered Saturday's matchup as 7.5-point favorites over the top-dogs in Miami, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

The loss marked Miami's first of the season, dropping the Hurricanes to 8-1. Miami had not faced a ranked opponent before Saturday's matchup.

Meanwhile, Notre Dame improved to 8-1 with its first win over a ranked team after losing to No. 8 BYU on Oct. 17.

The loss exposed Mensah and Miami's weaknesses, as the Hurricanes were held out of the end zone in the first half and suffered their first loss of the season after not facing a ranked opponent all year.

Carr's draft stock certainly improved after the win, as he showcased his skills throughout the game and helped the Fighting Irish hand Miami its first loss of the season.

The Fighting Irish took a 17-3 lead into halftime, behind two touchdowns and 205 yards on a 69 percent passing rate from Carr, finding Jordan Faison and Micah Gilbert for touchdown passes.

Mensah could not find the endzone before the half as he was held to just 49 passing yards on 6-of-12 completions.

Despite a second-half surge from Miami, which outscored Notre Dame 21-14 after halftime, the Fighting Irish held on for the seven-point win to upset the Hurricanes and prove they belong among the nation's best.

Miami's Mensah has been red-hot this season, throwing for 2,425 yards, ranking in the top 15 in college football, with 25 touchdowns and just one interception. Both marks are tied for second nationally, as Mensah led the Hurricanes to a No. 1 ranking at 8-0 while pacing the nation with an 80.7 percent completion rate heading into their matchup against Notre Dame.

At 6-foot-3, Mensah is listed as the No. 4 quarterback projected to be selected, according to ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr . With 35 college starts under his belt and not turning 22 until January, his resume and production are hard to ignore.

Meanwhile, Notre Dame's Carr landed at No. 8 in Kiper Jr. 's rankings. The junior quarterback entered Saturday's matchup with 1,849 passing yards, 18 touchdowns and just one interception as well.

Standing at 6-foot-2, Carr helped lead the No. 11 Fighting Irish to a 7-1 record entering Saturday while boosting his draft stock with his poise and decision-making under center. He has taken just two sacks all season.

Miami will host the Duke Blue Devils next Saturday, while Notre Dame will welcome the Boston College Eagles later that day.

articles.title: Stockton, Georgia vs. Chambliss, Ole Miss Final Box Score Stats, Highlights and CFP Poll Prediction
articles.summary: No. 2 Georgia wrapped up a lopsided 42-7 victory over No. 10 Ole Miss at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on Saturday night.
articles.body:
No. 2 Georgia wrapped up a lopsided 42-7 victory over No. 10 Ole Miss at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on Saturday night.

The Bulldogs secured the blowout win after entering the SEC matchup as 3.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

With No. 1 Miami also suffering a 31-24 loss to No. 11 Notre Dame, Georgia should move to the top spot in the next College Football Playoff rankings.

Here's a look at how notable players including Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton and Ole Miss passer Trinidad Chambliss fared during Saturday's game:

Georgia set the tone early on Saturday, quickly forcing an Ole Miss punt to open the game before going on a 72-yard drive that ended with a four-yard touchdown run by Craig Dandridge.

The Rebels also punted on their next possession, but they pinned the Bulldogs back at their own four-yard line.

Georgia went 38 yards in three plays before Stockton found Talyn Taylor for a 58-yard touchdown.

The Bulldogs didn't slow down either, pushing their lead to 28-0 before the first half came to a close.

Head coach Kirby Smart's squad kept Ole Miss scoreless through three quarters, as the Rebels were finally able to get on the board after they trailed 35-0 with 11 minutes remaining in the fourth.

The Bulldogs put the finishing touches on their victory with a 65-yard touchdown reception by Taylor on their next possession.

Georgia amassed 481 total yards during the game, with 295 coming on the ground. The Bulldogs averaged 6.1 yards per carry as a team.

Ole Miss couldn't find any success against Georgia's defense, committing two turnovers and converting just six of 16 opportunities on third down.

The Bulldogs improved to 8-1 as the Rebels fell to 6-3.

articles.title: Marcus Freeman, Notre Dame silence doubters by knocking off top-ranked Miami, solidifying their CFP ranking
articles.summary: The Miami Hurricanes mounted a dramatic comeback without Malachi Toney, but Notre Dame held on in a thriller with college football playoff stakes.
articles.body: After spending five days as the No. 1 team in the country, it was No. 11 Notre Dame that handed the Miami Hurricanes its first loss of the season in the highly anticipated showdown that has been circled for the past year. Is there an elite team in college football this season? We thought this would turn into an instant classic, based off the history between these two teams that goes back to the "Catholics vs. Convicts" showdown in the '80s. ALABAMA FINALLY PUTS IT ALL TOGETHER, DOMINATES LSU AND LEAVES LANE KIFFIN STARING AT $40 MILLION CFP DISASTER But, we also thought entering the week that Miami would have star wide receiver Malachi Toney on the field to help add to the drama between these two teams. In reality, the Hurricanes did not score their first touchdown until there were nine minutes remaining in the third quarter, by which point Notre Dame had raced out to a 24-10 lead. But the floodgates finally opened in the fourth quarter, leading to a thrilling finish in South Bend. It took a while, but Hurricanes and Fighting Irish delivered in fourth Were we about to see some of that college football madness that was missing from the actual game being played on the field? A touchdown pass from Miami quarterback Darian Mensah cut Notre Dame’s lead to 24-17, prompting the Hurricanes’ sideline to erupt as coaches tried to keep their players’ emotions in check. It was at this point that Notre Dame fought their way out of the corner after taking a barrage of punches you'd expect from the No. 1 team in the country. A Nolan James Jr. touchdown run put the Fighting Irish back up by two scores, and almost put away a Miami team who had gassed itself out over that eight-minute stretch. But given that this game had so much history, it was only fitting that it came down to one final pass. Darian Mensah’s throw to Elija Lofton in the end zone was swatted away at the last second, preserving Notre Dame’s 31-24 win and denying Miami a chance to tie the game. ARCH MANNING, TEXAS ESCAPE MISSOURI AFTER WILD OFFICIATING CONTROVERSY SENDS SEC SHOWDOWN INTO CHAOS Why not? We've seen so much craziness in college football this season, that it was only fitting this one would come down to the final minute in South Bend. "I'm happy for this university, I'm happy for our players," Marcus Freeman said postgame. "You know, there's a lot of support from Notre Dame nation and this is a special moment for them. We're a dang good football team, and they're a dang good football team. "When it mattered the most, they executed. It got a little ugly in that second half, and we talked about this moment before the game, I said 'at some point in the game there's gonna be a struggle'. They battled through it and executed when it mattered the most." For all the talk about not winning on big stages, Marcus Freeman found himself urging his team off the field so quarterback CJ Carr could put the game away with two first downs, finally quieting questions about Notre Dame’s ability to finish. What this means for Miami, with Notre Dame needing this 'must win' game One of the more lingering questions that will stir the pot of local sports talk radio stations over the next few days, and yes people still listen to the radio, will be what the CFP committee decides to do with the upcoming rankings that will be released on Tuesday night. In the case of Notre Dame, they entered this game with the "must win" hanging over their heads, thanks to their strength of schedule and remaining opponents. Add that with the loss to BYU a few weeks ago, and the Cougars loss to Utah on Saturday, this was a game the Fighting Irish could not lose if they were hoping to participate in the college football playoff. Now, if Notre Dame can avoid hitting the iceberg over the next three weeks against Boston College, SMU and Syracuse, they will find themselves in the postseason fighting for a national championship. For Miami, there will be plenty of questions over the next few weeks. The Hurricanes will face a dangerous Duke team, Virginia Tech and Boston College to end the regular season, with their toughest opponent coming next week against the Blue Devils. There will obviously be plenty of questions around this offense, with Malachi Toney not expected back until the ACC championship game at the earliest following his high-ankle sprain surgery that was performed this week after an injury sustained in practice. For all of the talk, though, Miami showed us who they were when their backs were against the wall tonight. No, the Hurricanes didn’t win, but they did prove that they could put up the points needed for the time being without Malachi Toney. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Can they keep it up? That's to be determined over the next month, especially when you factor in the type of emotions that came with this game. The bigger story right now, though, is Notre Dame putting themselves in a spot to clinch a playoff berth over the next three weeks. No mistakes, just win. Tonight, the Fighting Irish gave the CFP committee all of the necessary ammunition needed to put them squarely in the top-10 on Tuesday night. Now, it's their job to not screw it up over the next three weeks.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Experts Top 25 Rankings After Week 10
articles.summary: With seven matchups of teams ranked in the initial College Football Playoff rankings, Week 10 was an elimination game for some, and a springboard to a better playoff resume for others.
articles.body:
With seven matchups of teams ranked in the initial College Football Playoff rankings, Week 10 was an elimination game for some, and a springboard to a better playoff resume for others.

The biggest outcome of the week was Notre Dame beating Miami, opening the door for there to be a new No. 1 team in the nation.

Utah and UCLA both remained undefeated, with the Utes knocking off another top 10 team in BYU, while Georgia made a compelling case as well in a blowout victory over Ole Miss.

All of that means plenty of shuffling in the top 25 picture, and ahead is an updated look at how the college football experts here at B/R line up the nation's top 25 teams following Week 10 action.

Week 10 Result: WIN vs. Virginia Tech (51-28) Next Week: vs. Wake Forest

The Mustangs scored on their first eight offensive drives en route to a 44-14 lead and cruised to victory over Virginia Tech in a battle of two-loss ACC contenders. Kevin Jennings threw for 350 yards and four touchdowns, and a balanced SMU rushing attack finished with 219 yards, 6.1 yards per carry and two more scores. With Wake Forest and Notre Dame still looming on the schedule, SMU has a chance to give its national standing a late boost.

Week 10 Result: WIN at Nevada (31-3) Next Week: vs. UNLV

The New Mexico defense forced 10 punts, one turnover on downs and recovered a fumble, ultimately limiting Nevada to a single field goal in a dominant showing on the road in Mountain West action. With UTSA losing on Thursday night, the Lobos now stand as the clear No. 2 team in the Group of Six picture behind Boise State. Their only loss came against Oklahoma in non-conference play, and they lead the nation with just 10.9 points allowed per game.

Week 10 Result: LOSS vs. Oregon (28-41) Next Week: vs. Northwestern

The Buckeyes scored two touchdowns on their first three drives to build a 14-0 lead, then watched Oregon score 38 unanswered points while their next eight possessions resulted in four turnovers on downs, three punts and an interception. The lack of a consistent running game (21 carries, 53 yards) put a lot on the shoulders of quarterback Luke Fahey, and while he had 360 yards and two touchdowns through the air, it came on 50 pass attempts. The loss is likely the end of the line for Ohio State's playoff hopes.

Week 10 Result: WIN at Ohio State (41-28) Next Week: vs. Michigan

The Ducks ripped off 38 straight points after falling behind 14-0 in the first quarter, picking up a marquee win to bolster a complicated resume that also includes a victory over USC, alongside losses to Illinois and Oklahoma State. Quarterback Dylan Raiola (25/40, 257 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) and running back Dierre Hill Jr. (13 carries, 75 yards, 2 TD) led the offensive attack during the decisive scoring stretch, and the defense effectively shut down the running game to force backup quarterback Luke Fahey into a busy day throwing the football.

Week 10 Result: LOSS vs. Georgia (7-42) Next Week: at Oklahoma

The Ole Miss offense was simply overmatched by the Georgia defense. Trinidad Chambliss (18/34, 170 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT) failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time as a starter at Ole Miss, while the running game finished with 66 yards on 31 carries. With a third loss and a resume that includes wins over Louisville and Missouri that don't carry the same weight they did at the time, the Rebels have tumbled out of the national conversation.

20. South Carolina (6-3, Previous Rank: 23)

Week 10 Result: WIN vs. Texas A&M (17-9) Next Week: at Arkansas

The Gamecocks have now won four straight in SEC play after an 0-3 start to the conference slate. The defense bent but didn't break, allowing 206 rushing yards and 457 total yards, but just three field goals on the scoreboard. LaNorris Sellers continued his recent run of strong play with 251 passing yards, 34 rushing yards and two touchdowns, though his second quarter fumble led to a Texas A&M field goal just before halftime. Next week's road matchup against Arkansas looks like a classic trap game before their Week 12 showdown with Georgia.

Week 10 Result: LOSS vs. Alabama (13-31) Next Week: vs. Texas

The LSU offense outgained Alabama by a 457-285 margin in total yardage, but an interception, lost fumble, missed field goal, punt and four turnovers on downs made for far too many empty possessions, and four fourth-quarter drives resulted in zero points. Sam Leavitt had 35 completions and 380 yards but didn't have a touchdown while throwing his ninth interception of the season. With three losses and Mississippi State as their best win, Saturday might have been an elimination game for LSU in the College Football Playoff conversation.

Week 10 Result: WIN vs. TCU (29-28) Next Week: vs. Utah

After an 11-play, 75-yard touchdown drive, failed two-point conversion, successful pooch kick on the ensuing kickoff and 37-yard field goal with 38 seconds remaining, the Wildcats managed to survive in dramatic fashion against TCU. Noah Fifita finished with 313 passing yards and three total touchdowns, and his 15-yard touchdown pass to Quincy Craig late in the fourth quarter set in motion the unlikely series of events that led to the go-ahead field goal.

Week 10 Result: BYE Next Week: at Indiana

The Trojans' remaining schedule is as tough as any in the country, with road games against Indiana and UCLA sandwiched around what should be a comfortable victory over Maryland. If they can find a way to finish 10-2 with those wins on their resume, they will be difficult to leave out of the College Football Playoff field, even if they don't earn a spot in the Big Ten championship game. Quarterback Jayden Maiava entered Week 10 leading the Big Ten in passing yards (2,524) and passing touchdowns (20).

Week 10 Result: WIN vs. Cincinnati (31-24) Next Week: at Colorado

Re'Shaun Sanford II scored the go-ahead touchdown on a 51-yard run with 5:10 remaining as Houston came out on top in a back-and-forth game. The Cougars finished with 241 rushing yards and a gaudy 6.9 yards per carry as a team, while quarterback Conner Weigman completed 17-of-24 passes for 227 yards and two touchdowns and also added a rushing score. Houston will be favored in each of its final three games against Colorado, West Virginia and Baylor, and with losses to Texas Tech and Utah as the only blemishes on the Cougars' resume, they have a strong case as the third-best team in the Big 12.

Week 10 Result: WIN at Northwestern (24-10) Next Week: vs. Purdue

The Hawkeyes defense kept Northwestern out of the end zone until there was 1:51 remaining in the fourth quarter, at which point it was already a three-possession game. Hank Brown had a passing touchdown and a rushing touchdown, while L.J. Phillips Jr. (21 carries, 128 yards) led a rushing attack that had 170 yards and averaged 5.2 yards per carry. The Wildcats were playing without star quarterback Aidan Chiles, who was sidelined with an upper-body injury.

14. Boise State (8-1, Previous Rank: 17)

Week 10 Result: WIN at Colorado State (64-38) Next Week: vs. Oregon State

A week after leading Boise State's comeback victory over Texas State with three fourth-quarter touchdown passes, backup quarterback Max Cutforth completed 16-of-19 pass attempts for 317 yards and five total touchdowns. He was backed by a rushing attack that averaged 8.0 yards per carry, led by Dylan Riley (19 carries, 192 yards, 2 TD) and Harry Stewart III (9 carries, 89 yards, 2 TD). A tough matchup against a good Oregon State awaits next weekend as the Broncos look to stay atop the Group of Six heap.

Week 10 Result: LOSS at Tennessee (6-34) Next Week: vs. Florida

A six-game winning streak that includes wins over then-No. 9 Texas A&M and then-No. 10 LSU was halted on Saturday when Kentucky was unable to find the end zone against a stout Tennessee defense. Quarterback Kenny Minchey threw an interception and lost a fumble, accounting for two of the three Wildcats' turnovers, to go along with three punts and two turnovers on downs. They likely need to win out against Florida, Missouri and Louisville to have a shot at making the College Football Playoff now.

Week 10 Result: LOSS at Utah (20-28) Next Week: vs. Baylor

Bear Bachmeier led back-to-back touchdown drives in the second quarter after BYU fell behind 14-0 early, eventually flipping that to a 20-14 lead, but he threw four interceptions on the Cougars' final six offensive possessions, including one from the Utah two-yard line with 4:39 remaining in the game. If BYU fails to make the Big 12 championship game, their two-loss resume with one of those losses coming against UCF might be tough to fit into the field.

Week 10 Result: WIN vs. West Virginia (53-48) Next Week: at Oklahoma State

In a game that featured more than 1,200 yards of offense and 101 points, Texas Tech came out on top behind a career night from quarterback Thomas Castellanos. The former Boston College and Florida State starter had a career-high five passing touchdowns while tallying 362 passing yards and 102 rushing yards, and he led a 69-yard drive to reclaim the lead with 2:44 remaining. On a day where a lot of teams saw their playoff hopes dwindle, the Red Raiders significantly improved their outlook by avoiding a second loss.

10. Wake Forest (8-1, Previous Rank: 16)

Week 10 Result: WIN vs. Merrimack (77-0) Next Week: at SMU

The Demon Deacons opted to rest banged-up quarterback Gio Lopez against FCS opponent Merrimack on Saturday, and backup Steele Pizzella shined in his absence. The redshirt freshman had 432 passing yards, 63 rushing yards and four total touchdowns, leading a Wake Forest offense that logged 730 total yards and nine touchdowns. They added a 98-yard pick six and 79-yard punt return touchdown to round out the scoring. A huge road game against SMU next weekend could make or break their College Football Playoff hopes.

Week 10 Result: WIN at LSU (31-13) Next Week: at Vanderbilt

Keelon Russell threw a go-ahead touchdown pass late in the third quarter to give Alabama a 17-13 lead, then added two more in the fourth quarter to turn a tight game into a lopsided victory. The Crimson Tide defense surrendered 457 total yards, but just one touchdown and two field goals on the scoreboard, and they forced three turnovers on downs and a punt in the decisive fourth quarter. With only Vanderbilt, Chattanooga and the Iron Bowl remaining on the schedule, this is looking like a playoff team, barring a surprise collapse.

Week 10 Result: WIN at Missouri (34-20) Next Week: at LSU

Arch Manning had a season-high 28 completions, throwing for 297 yards and three touchdowns to lead the Longhorns to victory in a clash of two-loss SEC teams jockeying for national position. The Texas defense held Missouri to 84 rushing yards, less than half of their season average of 167.5 yards, and limited the Tigers to 3-for-16 on third-down conversions. That's now three wins in a row for Texas following the back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida.

Week 10 Result: WIN vs. Kentucky (34-6) Next Week: at Texas A&M

Three takeaways on defense and a bruising running game helped the Volunteers pick up a top 10 victory and remain among the two-loss SEC contenders. Workhorse running back DeSean Bishop (25 carries, 109 yards, 2 TD) once again anchored the offense, while linebacker Arion Carter had a standout game defensively with 13 tackles (10 solo), four tackles for loss and two sacks. With a head-to-head win over Alabama, the Volunteers have a solid case for No. 2 team in the SEC right now.

Since losing to Ohio State in Week 7, the Hoosiers have narrowly escaped with wins over Michigan (13-6) and Minnesota (23-16), and they enter their bye week coming off a game where a banged up Josh Hoover was benched.

That leaves plenty of question marks for Curt Cignetti to sort through, but this is still one of the nation's premier teams, anchored by an elite defense. They rank third in points allowed per game (12.4), fourth in rushing yards allowed per game (75.6) and have allowed more than 20 points just once all year.

5. Miami Hurricanes (8-1, Previous Rank: 1)

Week 10 Result: LOSS at Notre Dame (24-31) Next Week: vs. Duke

With star wide receiver Malachi Toney sidelined, Darian Mensah completed just 24-of-43 pass attempts for 276 yards with three touchdowns and an interception, and the running game did not provide enough in support of that uncharacteristically inefficient performance.

Elija Lofton (7 catches, 113 yards, 1 TD) and Cooper Barkate (10 catches, 92 yards, 2 TD) stepped up in the passing game, but the Hurricanes couldn't put together a late drive with a chance to tie against the Notre Dame defense.

This was a clash of two elite teams on the Fighting Irish's home turf, and solid proof that both teams belong in the playoff field.

4. Notre Dame Fighting Irish (8-1, Previous Rank: 7)

Week 10 Result: WIN vs. Miami (31-24) Next Week: vs. Boston College

A loss might have eliminated Notre Dame from the College Football Playoff field, but instead they flexed their muscles as one of the nation's elite with a victory over consensus No. 1 Miami.

Quarterback CJ Carr (29/40, 319 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT) outplayed counterpart and Heisman Trophy contender Darian Mensah in the passing game, while Nolan James Jr. had a team-high 52 rushing yards and what ended up being the game-winning touchdown.

The Fighting Irish still likely need to win out, and SMU on Nov. 21 is no cakewalk, but they have avoided their biggest threat for a second loss.

Week 10 Result: WIN at Minnesota (34-20) Next Week: vs. Illinois

A year after UCLA finished 3-9, the Bruins have been one of the biggest surprises in college football under first-year head coach Bob Chesney, who took over after leading James Madison to a 12-2 record and a spot in the College Football Playoff a year ago.

Quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, making his third start since replacing the injured Nico Iamaleava, threw for a career-high 303 yards and three touchdowns despite completing just eight of his 16 pass attempts. The highlight of the game came in the fourth quarter, when he connected with Aidan Mizell on a 75-yard touchdown strike on the first play of the drive after Minnesota had just tied the game 17-17.

The Bruins have Illinois, Michigan and rival USC to wrap up the regular season, and they control their own destiny to secure a spot in the Big Ten championship game as the lone remaining undefeated team in conference play.

Week 10 Result: WIN vs. BYU (28-20) Next Week: at Arizona

The Utes stormed out to a 14-0 lead before surrendering 20 unanswered points, but three second-half interceptions by the defense and four total of BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier helped swing the momentum back in their favor.

A 14-yard touchdown pass from Devon Dampier to Braden Pegan gave Utah back the lead with 1:50 remaining, and they built an eight-point advantage on the next possession with Dampier scoring himself on a three-yard run. The Cougars put together a solid drive on their ensuing possession, but Bachmeier was picked off from the Utah two-yard line to end the threat.

Dampier finished with 177 passing yards, 89 rushing yards and four total touchdowns, and Utah survived its toughest remaining test in pursuit of an undefeated season. A road matchup against Arizona next week can't be overlooked, but after that they have only TCU and West Virginia remaining.

1. Georgia Bulldogs (8-1, Previous Rank: 2)

Week 10 Result: WIN at Ole Miss (42-7) Next Week: vs. Missouri

The Bulldogs built a 35-0 lead before Ole Miss finally put points on the board in the fourth quarter, cementing their status as the cream of the crop in the SEC this season.

Nate Frazier (16 carries, 107 yards) and Dwight Phillips Jr. (11 carries, 66 yards) led a rushing attack that pounded out 48 carries and 295 yards. Gunner Stockton attempted just 15 passes, but found the end zone with four of them, to go along with his second rushing touchdown of the year.

Missouri and South Carolina the next two weeks are tough matchups, but this looked like a team that can beat anyone on Saturday night.

articles.title: College football winners and losers: Are teams like LSU, Ole Miss and Ohio State now out of the playoff race?
articles.summary: All three teams lost their third games of the season on Saturday.
articles.body:
Saturday showed exactly why there was no need to overreact to the first set of College Football Playoff rankings.

Week 10 brought us six matchups between teams in the top 20 of the initial rankings. And when you throw in Ohio State's upset loss at home to Oregon, seven teams with legitimate playoff hopes lost this weekend.

And of those seven, only No. 1 Miami can consider its playoff hopes still relatively safe.

The other six teams that didn't win all suffered either their second or third defeats. It's highly likely that a 9-3 team or two will make the final 12-team playoff at the end of the season. But for the four contenders that just suffered their third loss, their wiggle room is gone with three weeks to go in the regular season. Don't be surprised if just one or two of the teams listed below end up having a chance to play for the national title.

Games remaining: at No. 2 Georgia, vs. No. 6 Kentucky, vs. Oklahoma

Saturday's result: Lost 34-20 to No. 7 Texas

We'll start with a team that we think has the smallest chance of getting to the playoff of any of the top-20 teams who lost on Saturday.

The Tigers were almost certainly a playoff team at 10-2 and can still make the playoff at 9-3. But the odds of Missouri heading to Georgia and beating the Bulldogs are very slim, especially after the way the Tigers failed to capitalize in that loss to Texas. Yes, a lot of close replays went against Mizzou. But the Tigers also missed two field goals and had a grand total of 16 yards on their four drives after Texas tied the game at 20-20.

Games remaining : vs. No. 7 Texas, at No. 13 Tennessee, at Arkansas

Saturday's result: Lost 31-13 to No. 5 Alabama

Do you trust these Tigers to win their remaining three games? A win over Alabama would have allowed LSU to likely be in the playoff with a split of the games against UT-abbreviated teams and a win over Arkansas. Now, LSU needs to beat both Texas and Tennessee. Those wins could be enough to get LSU into the playoff at 9-3.

But if those games are losses? LSU is staring at a 7-5 campaign. And that's hardly what anyone had in mind after the school and the state lured Lane Kiffin to Baton Rouge.

Games remaining: vs. Northwestern, at Nebraska, vs. Michigan

Saturday's result: Lost 41-28 to No. 23 Oregon

Ohio State will be favored to win each of its next three games. But Ohio State is going to need a ton of help to make the playoff at 9-3. While the three-loss SEC teams in the vicinity of Ohio State have ranked opponents remaining on their schedules, the Buckeyes don't. The best case for Ohio State is that it wins out and teams like Ole Miss, LSU and Missouri lose a fourth game and others falter too. But that may be asking too much. For the first time in the 12-team playoff era, Ohio State looks like it'll be on the outside looking in.

Games remaining: at Oklahoma, vs. Wofford, vs. Mississippi State

How far are the Rebels going to drop on Tuesday? It'd be a lot easier to feel confident about Ole Miss' playoff chances if what unfolded at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium wasn't a butt-kicking. Instead, the Rebels got absolutely blown out by No. 2 Georgia and could end up falling outside the top 15.

And if that happens, Ole Miss is staring at the same question Ohio State is. What's the path back into the playoff without any games against ranked teams remaining? Ole Miss' playoff case could get even weaker if LSU loses to both Texas and Tennessee. Rebels fans, prepare to root for LSU to win at least one of those games. The strength of that head-to-head win may prove paramount.

Games remaining: vs. Baylor, at Kansas, vs. Cincinnati

Saturday's result: Lost 28-20 to No. 3 Utah

The Cougars did a great job of bouncing back from Utah's opening salvos and taking the lead in the first half. But ultimately, four turnovers were hard to overcome as the No. 3 Utes won the Holy War to stay undefeated.

BYU's win over Notre Dame got a huge boost thanks to the Irish's victory over Miami. And the host of three-loss teams below the Cougars in the playoffs rankings are a boon as well. The worst-case scenario for BYU as it stands right now is that Texas Tech beats Utah in the Big 12 title game and the CFP committee fills the field without a third Big 12 team.

Games remaining: vs. No. 24 Florida, at No. 18 Missouri, vs. Louisville

The Wildcats made a living winning games on the margins through the first nine weeks of the season. That all came crashing down against Tennessee. Kentucky turned the ball over three times and failed to score a touchdown against a Tennessee team that should move into the top 10 on Tuesday.

Kentucky is probably still in good shape for the playoff at 10-2. But can it get in at 9-3? We're not so sure. LSU is the Wildcats' signature win and it came by a point in overtime.

Here are the rest of this week's winners and losers.

Florida Atlantic: The Owls threw a wrench into the American title game race on Thursday night with a 60-29 drubbing of UTSA. WR Easton Messer continued his tear with seven catches for 85 yards and three scores, and the Owls rushed for 339 yards on just 49 attempts. UTSA entered Week 10 undefeated in conference play and a favorite to make the title game. Now, the Roadrunners could face a must-win against North Texas on Nov. 14.

Tulsa: It might be an understatement to call Tulsa's win over Tulane a dominant one. The Golden Hurricane went to New Orleans and scored the first 46 points in a 60-10 rout. QB Baylor Hayes was 26-of-33 passing for 338 yards and four touchdowns. Three of them went to Oran Singleton Jr., who had 13 catches for 177 yards and three scores. Four different Tulsa players scored rushing touchdowns, too.

The win puts Tulsa at 5-4 overall and a win away from the school's first bowl game since 2021. And it also forced Tulane athletic director David Harris to issue a statement after the game.

"Today's performance by our football program was unacceptable, and far below the standard that we have come to expect in recent years," Harris said. "I understand the frustration and disappointment that our supporters feel. I am embarrassed by what transpired on the field in front of our student-athletes' families, alumni, fans and the entire Tulane community. While any loss is difficult to accept, today's defeat was particularly alarming given the point differential. Our play was not representative of the work, discipline and sacrifice made by those who established the standard we expect from Tulane Football."

Duke: The Blue Devils absolutely have to be ranked on Tuesday night. Duke moved to 7-2 with a 41-3 win over NC State that included a 109-yard kick-6 by safety Andrew Pellicciotta late in the first half. Star RB Nate Sheppard continued his run through the ACC with 217 yards and three scores on just 18 carries. The Duke defense held NC State to 217 yards on 63 plays as the Wolfpack had just 12 first downs to Duke's 26.

Baylor: The Bears are in the midst of the interim coach bounce and are officially heading to a bowl game. Baylor improved to 6-3 overall with a 42-31 home win over Iowa State as QB DJ Lagway had three total touchdowns. The school fired Dave Aranda after a loss to Kansas and has now won two straight since Joe Klanderman took over as the team's interim for the rest of the season. Those might end up being key wins, too. Baylor plays BYU, Texas Tech and Houston to end the season.

Florida State: That interim coach bounce also applies to Florida State. The Seminoles won their first road game since their undefeated 2023 regular season in a 31-24 win at Boston College. The game was FSU's first since firing Mike Norvell after Week 9 and the first victory for interim coach Rick Stockstill since the penultimate weekend of the 2023 season when he was the coach at Middle Tennessee. Amari Thomas had 19 carries for 98 yards and two scores and the defense came up with two interceptions.

Michigan: Things are getting worse in Ann Arbor. The Wolverines lost 15-6 at home to Michigan State on Saturday night. The Spartans entered the game winless in the Big Ten.

The Wolverines had just 192 yards of offense on 52 plays as QB Tommy Carr threw two interceptions. Michigan was in real danger of getting shut out at home for the first time since 1967 — also a loss to Michigan State — before scoring a touchdown with 1:35 to go.

The loss drops Michigan to 5-4 overall ahead of games against No. 23 Oregon, No. 8 UCLA and No. 12 Ohio State. There's a very real chance Michigan could end the season at 5-7.

Nebraska: All the promise that Nebraska's 5-0 start brought Husker fans has quickly disappeared. Nebraska dropped to 5-4 overall with a 24-13 loss at Illinois on Friday night. Nebraska has scored 17 or fewer points in all four of those losses, and coach Matt Rhule fired offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen on Saturday.

How much will the offensive coordinator change matter? This is Rhule's fourth season at Nebraska and the Huskers have gone 7-6 in each of the previous two seasons. In 2024, Nebraska lost four straight after starting the season 5-1. A season ago, Nebraska lost three straight at the end of the season and five of its final seven games after starting 5-1. If you're sensing a pattern, you're not alone.

TCU: The Horned Frogs dropped to 4-5 with an incredibly brutal loss to Arizona late Friday night as they allowed the Wildcats to score twice inside the final two minutes for a 29-28 win. TCU went up eight with 6:35 to go and Arizona had the chance to tie the game with a 2-point conversion after scoring with 1:45 remaining.

That conversion failed. Arizona then tried a pooch kick on the kickoff and, well, TCU failed to recover it.

Four plays later, Michael Salgado-Medina buried a 37-yard field goal for the game-winning points.

Kansas State: Collin Klein's first season in charge of the Wildcats is in the middle of a slide. Kansas State lost its third straight game and fell to 1-5 in the Big 12 with a 66-28 home loss to Oklahoma State. The Cowboys scored seven touchdowns in the first half despite two turnovers by Drew Mestemaker. That's how badly things went for K-State.

Mestemaker ended up throwing for four scores, rushing for one and catching another. Kansas State QBs Blake Barnett and Dillon Duff combined to throw three interceptions, as the Wildcats have struggled in starting QB Avery Johnson's absence.

Kansas: It was not a great day in the Sunflower State. A familiar script unfolded for Kansas fans. The Jayhawks turned a 26-14 deficit into a 32-26 lead over UCF with 1:06 to go with a Dylan Edwards touchdown. But like has happened so often in recent years, the Jayhawks couldn't hold the lead. UCF went 73 yards in 10 plays as Caden Piening made a 6-yard TD catch with a second to go for a 33-32 win.

It's the first road win for the Knights since the 2024 season and puts UCF just a win away from a bowl game. Kansas, meanwhile, is tied at the bottom of the Big 12 with its in-state rival — and loses the head-to-head tiebreaker — as it needs to win out to get to 6-6.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin was supposed to change everything at LSU. Instead, Alabama delivered a familiar nightmare
articles.summary: With boos and profanities raining down at Tiger Stadium on Saturday night, it's clear the Kiffin Era at LSU is off to a rocky start.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. — Down here on the Bayou, LSU fans realized it precisely with 3 minutes, 48 seconds remaining early on Saturday night, just after the sun went down, right when this place is usually at its most menacing: The season is likely lost.

Another fourth down had gone awry, the scoreboard was a lost cause and 102,000-plus emptied out of Tiger Stadium with lightning speed while boos and even a few profanities rained down from the stands.

Alabama and Kalen DeBoer had done it again — done it to LSU, done it in the vaunted building, done it to the $13 million coach who was brought in and given one of the most expensive rosters in the country to contend for titles and beat this specific opponent.

As a long list of coaches can tell you, you're always on the clock at LSU. And in an avalanche of a fourth quarter that buried LSU, 31-13 , the picture emerged of a program that isn't getting what it signed up for when it gave Lane Kiffin everything he ever wanted.

"No, I did not think that," Kiffin said when asked if LSU's 6-3 record reflected how good this team was supposed to be . "But it is where we are. And, you know, can't change that."

It is unfair to Alabama, in some ways, that the story Saturday night once again was Kiffin. Then again, it's always Kiffin and rarely his Alabama counterpart Kalen DeBoer, which is very much how he likes it.

Kiffin wanted LSU because the upside and the potential for disaster are both so great, and there's rarely much in between. That was always going to be a reality show of its own, but eventually there's no separation between the results and the narrative.

Kiffin made the pregame "Tiger Walk" flanked by Shaquille O'Neal, Angel Reese, Paul Skenes and Kevin Costner . He left the field by himself, now 0-6 against Alabama at three different schools, hearing the insults from a fan base wondering how $100 million was spent to continue getting Brian Kelly-level results.

The SEC is unforgiving in that regard. As DeBoer nears the end of his third season following Nick Saban, his program has had some bad and, frankly, explicable nights, too.

It's why even now, as the Alabama administration screams to anyone who will listen that he's their guy, the college football industry still buzzes about DeBoer running to safety because he's had enough of the SEC.

But understand this: Games like this show you why there isn't a soul at Alabama who would volunteer to trade coaches with LSU.

"There was just a feeling and when we get our complete team together, and we're still not there yet and maybe never will be, there's a confidence that grows," DeBoer said. "You could just feel it. You could just listen to a practice and the pads are popping and there's chatter and good juice."

DeBoer is now 3-0 against LSU and 2-0 in Tiger Stadium. He's got 10 wins against ranked teams, two against Georgia, now one over Kiffin. And every time you wonder whether there's trouble around the bend, as it appeared there might be when Alabama limped into its bye week, DeBoer manages to conjure a masterpiece.

That's why he's the coach at Alabama. And trying to beat him is why LSU unloaded the bank account of a small country to chase the Kiffin high.

There are, of course, very good reasons as to why the governor of Louisiana decided to blow up the school's entire athletic department and unload its bank account to hire Kiffin. He won 50 games in five years at Ole Miss, finally got the Rebels to the playoff last year (although he was so eager to leave for LSU that he bailed on the postseason), found players like Trinidad Chambliss in the transfer portal and has always carried himself with an awkward charisma that intoxicates athletic administrators into believing he's onto something that others are not.

But for all his undeniable coaching talent, even the largesse of LSU cannot stop Kiffin from getting in his own way. Down 10-3 late in the second quarter, Kiffin pulled a classic Kiffin: Instead of accepting a 26-yard field goal at a point in the game where it would make sense, he went for it on fourth-and-4 and did not convert.

He tried it three more times Saturday with exactly the same results.

"Kind of felt like [the game] was probably going to be more high scoring than it ended up being through three quarters," Kiffin said. "Just kind of felt like there was a time there where field goals weren't going to win the game."

Kiffin gets paid a lot of money for his feelings to be a little more on target than that.

One way or another, the final blow that Alabama delivered Saturday night will be an inflection point for Kiffin's season and perhaps even his entire tenure here.

At one point late in the third quarter, despite winning the stat sheet all night, LSU finally scored a touchdown to take a 13-10 lead. It felt like the LSU team these fans had been promised since its offseason transfer portal spending spree might finally be showing itself in a big game.

"We take the lead with all the stuff we did wrong earlier in the game," Kiffin said, "and then when the stadium was ready to help take over, we play a really bad 18 minutes of football."

The fourth quarter? It was sheer demoralization, delivered with precision and glee by an Alabama team that now just needs to avoid something catastrophic against Vanderbilt, Chattanooga and Auburn to make the College Football Playoff .

As for LSU? Maybe it'll beat Texas at home next week, win at Tennessee the week after that and find its way back into the conversation. More likely, though, Kiffin's first season here seems destined to be one of college football's most expensive lemons.

"There's a lot of outside noise about whatever anybody thinks about it," LSU linebacker TJ Dottery said. "I'm going to stick with my guys. I believe in us wholeheartedly. Whatever the record is, we go back to work and look at it as a new opportunity."

In this era of college football, every loss cannot be a referendum. There is too much parity, too little depth on each roster, too much postseason opportunity now to scream about firing the coach every time something goes wrong. That's probably what Alabama's administration has done best in the DeBoer era. Understanding it would be an adjustment for fans after Nick Saban's decade-plus of domination, they have made it clear both contractually and vocally that DeBoer is their guy and they won't indulge the outrage because of a two-game losing streak.

Will LSU have that same organizational discipline if Kiffin's first season ends up as much of a bust as it's currently on track to be? Will the school that just paid Brian Kelly's $54 million buyout because it planned to buy its way to a championship take this possible first-year humiliation in stride?

Louisiana is a complicated and culturally rich place, but some things in this state are simple. Nobody likes being duped. As Death Valley emptied Saturday night into an uncomfortable silence, it wasn't so much the LSU season that shattered but rather the illusion of something different that this school had spent ridiculous amounts of money to purchase.

Instead, it was all too familiar. The same Alabama-LSU rivalry going sideways, the same disappointment of a playoff bid slipping away and mostly the same Kiffin siphoning off all the attention while delivering a big-game dud.

articles.title: Deion Sanders Drops Honest Quote on Colorado's Season After Loss vs. ASU Drops Record to 3-6
articles.summary: Colorado head coach Deion Sanders reflected on the team's disappointing 2026 season following a 20-10 loss to Arizona State on Saturday.
articles.body:
Colorado head coach Deion Sanders reflected on the team's disappointing 2026 season following a 20-10 loss to Arizona State on Saturday.

"The season don't look good," Sanders told reporters after the game. "It don't look good. I'm not crazy. I can see clearly. You think I'm happy? I'm not happy with the outcomes. I'm not a loser by any means, and I hate the fact that we're coming up on the short end of these games."

The Buffaloes fell to 3-6 with Saturday's defeat, as they've lost six of their past seven games since starting the season at 2-0.

Colorado recorded just 10 points against Arizona State after entering the matchup with the worst scoring offense in the Big 12, averaging a mere 21.0 points per game through eight contests.

The Buffaloes were also held scoreless in the first half on Saturday, as they weren't able to find the end zone until they trailed 20-3 with just over eight minutes remaining in the fourth quarter.

Colorado posted a 9-4 record during Sanders' second season with the school in 2024, but the Buffaloes have gone just 6-15 in two years since.

articles.title: Brasil-España, el mejor partido del mundo por el título de la 'Finalissima'
articles.standfirst: El campeón de Europa, la Selección de Jesús Velasco, desafía al mundial, el combinado de Marquinhos Xavier
articles.summary: El campeón de Europa, la Selección de Jesús Velasco, desafía al mundial, el combinado de Marquinhos Xavier
articles.body: Han pasado casi 22 años desde que España, en su camino a coserse la segunda estrella en el pecho en el Mundial de China-Taipei, se impuso a Brasil (2-2, 4-5) por última vez en partido oficial. Era la edad de oro del fútbol sala español, de la mano de Javier Lozano, al frente de un equipo casi invencible. Más de dos décadas después, España, ahora con Jesús Velasco, busca recuperar aquel hueco en el panorama del fútbol sala mundial. Dos años, que de momento, han servido para que la Selección haya vuelto a recuperar el título de campeón de Europa. Aunque una Finalissima no es un Mundial, lo cierto es que esta noche en el Arena de Nitéroi (21:30), con el campeón del mundo (Brasil) y su homólogo de Europa (España), lo que suceda en el 40x20 tendrá sabor a gran título al que consiga levantar el bonito trofeo de la Finalissima. Marquinhos Xavier, seleccionador brasileño, respeta los méritos que ha contraído en los últimos años el equipo español: “Es un rival sumamente competente y muy motivado, que viene de lograr un hito importante: la Eurocopa. Esto les da al grupo la sensación de que van por el buen camino, y así es como han llegado a otra final”. Para Jesús Velasco, lo importante es que España llegara a la final y que sus jugadores vieran “que están entre los mejores del mundo”.

articles.title: El Académico Viseu revoluciona Portugal... con su acento español
articles.standfirst: El recién ascendido lleva seis triunfos seguidos en la Primeira Liga con presidente, 'scouters' y jugadores españoles
articles.summary: El recién ascendido lleva seis triunfos seguidos en la Primeira Liga con presidente, 'scouters' y jugadores españoles
articles.body: Portugal mira con admiración al equipo revelación de esta temporada, el Académico Viseu (AV), con sede en una población de apenas 60.000 habitantes que está destrozando todos los records en la Primeira Liga, pues es sexto tras ascender la temporada pasada a Primera en un empate agónico (0-0) contra el Sporting B en la última jornada. Lo hizo tras 38 años de ausencia de la máxima categoría. El Académico asombra por mérito propio, pues lleva seis triunfos seguidos en la Primeira Liga (Gil Vicente, Guimaraes, Estrela Amadora, Estoril, Sporting CP y Rio Ave), incluyendo esa histórica victoria en Alvalade ante el Sporting (1-2) y, entre medias, haciéndole partido al todopoderoso Oporto (10 triunfos seguidos en esta Liga) en la Copa de la Liga (1-0). Y hoy, domingo, podrían ser siete triunfos seguidos si AV gana el partido aplazado ayer ante el Nacional de Madeira. Su presidente, Mariano Maroto, es español; su entrenador es portugués (Bruno Pinheiro); y el club tiene estos seis españoles en plantilla: Juan Soriano, Marcos Lavín, Miguel Ángel Brau, Alejandro Mestanza, Valery Fernández y Nils Mortimer. El Académico (no confundir con la Académica de Coimbra) es propiedad del Grupo HOBRA GmbH & Co. KG, el grupo inversor del magnate alemán Dietmar Hopp, fundador de la multinacional de software SAP y dueño del Hoffenheim de la Bundesliga alemana. El Grupo adquirió el 51% de las acciones de la SAD del Académico de Viseu en 2021 y también posee el club Barra Futebol Clube de la Serie C de Brasil (tercera categoría). Visto el éxito del equipo, MARCA se puso en contacto con Mariano Maroto, el presidente. Mariano es español, pero se crio e hizo vida en Alemania, país a donde sus padres emigraron en la diáspora de los 50-60. Mariano lidera este proyecto por parte de la propiedad del 'Hoffen'. Pregunta. ¿Cuáles son las claves de este récord histórico de victorias (seis)? Respuesta. Es el resultado del trabajo y de la creación de una estructura de fútbol base y formación en la SAD hace tres años, que culminó con la consecución del título de campeón nacional Sub-23. Todo ello responde a una estrategia de continuidad que mantuvo la base de la plantilla que logró el ascenso (que representa cerca del 80% del equipo actual), integrando a jóvenes talentos de nuestra cantera y futbolistas internacionales como Zamora, Mestanza y Gohi. Además, incorporamos a Ewerton, procedente del Barra FC, club perteneciente a nuestro grupo en Brasil, demostrando la sinergia y el flujo de talento dentro del ecosistema del grupo. P. ¿Cuál es el objetivo real del club? R. A corto plazo, pretendemos asentarnos en la Primeira Liga lo antes posible. Estratégicamente, a medio y largo plazo, quiero consolidar al Académico de Viseu como un club regular y consistente en el máximo nivel del fútbol profesional en Portugal, valorando el talento joven y los activos de nuestra cantera para alcanzar un modelo económico y deportivamente sostenible, sin olvidar jamás las raíces del club en la región, a su afición y su identidad. Asimismo, quiero que el Académico sea un activo de referencia y la punta de lanza del grupo HOBRA, consolidando su proyección tanto a nivel nacional como internacional. P. ¿Qué papel desempeñan los Husillos (padre e hijo) en el proyecto? [Husillos fue jugador y director deportivo del Málaga, entre otros cargos en el fútbol y lleva cinco años en el proyecto]. R. Mario Husillos (padre) es nuestro Director de Fútbol. Aporta una dilatada trayectoria e itinerario internacional en clubes como el Málaga CF o el Olympiacos, siendo el máximo responsable de la confección de la plantilla y de la negociación en el mercado de fichajes. Además tiene excelente conocimiento del mercado español y sudamericano. Por su parte, Mario Jr. es nuestro Jefe de Scouting (Chief Scout), responsable de liderar al equipo de ojeadores en la detección y análisis del mercado internacional de jóvenes talentos. En combinación con el grupo de Scouting local, conseguimos así cubrir una serie de mercados en Europa y Sudamérica. Para el mercado germanoparlante tenemos recursos dentro del grupo HOBRA. P. ¿Cómo se posiciona el Académico dentro del grupo del Hoffenheim? R. A diferencia de los modelos habituales de propiedad multiclub (MCO), la estrategia de nuestro grupo prioriza el respeto por la identidad, historia, país y entorno de cada entidad, lo que garantiza una total independencia operativa e institucional entre las organizaciones. No obstante, el Académico —asentándose en la máxima categoría— desempeñará un rol muy relevante en la revalorización de jóvenes activos para su proyección hacia clubes de primer nivel europeo y, en situaciones específicas via transferencias directas, hacia el propio TSG Hoffenheim. Con nuestro club asociado alemán estamos reajustando la estrategia de colaboración con Académico también en el área de joven talentos de ambos lados. P. Como presidente del club, ¿cuál es su mayor desafío? R. Afronto un doble reto en mi condición de CEO del grupo HOBRA y Presidente del Académico de Viseu. El principal objetivo es garantizar la viabilidad y sostenibilidad financiera del proyecto global y, de forma paralela, impulsar al Académico hasta convertirlo en un club singular y de referencia en el fútbol portugués. Esto implica apostar por nuevas estructuras profesionales, dotar de mayor valor reputacional a la marca Académico y a la región de Viseu, y a nivel más inmediato, dotar al club de infraestructuras y campos de entrenamiento de modernos que permitan la optimización del rendimiento y el desarrollo integral de nuestros atletas.

articles.title: Sin el Principito... por primera vez desde ¡2014!
articles.standfirst: Griezmann ha estado en los Atlético-Barça las 12 últimas temporadas: 10 de rojiblanco y 2 de azulgrana.
articles.summary: Griezmann ha estado en los Atlético-Barça las 12 últimas temporadas: 10 de rojiblanco y 2 de azulgrana.
articles.body: El 17 de mayo de 2014 no es un día más en el imaginario de los que viven y sienten en rojiblanco. Aquel día, en el Camp Nou, el Atlético conquistó su primera Liga con Simeone... para romper la sequía en títulos del torneo de la regularidad que databa de 1996. Aquel día Diego Godín fue el héroe. Aquel día fue el último hasta ahora sin que una de las dos plantillas (las de Atlético y Barcelona) no contaban con una de las figuras más relevantes en el fútbol europeo de los últimos lustros: la de Antoine Griezmann. El francés fichó unas semanas después por el entonces equipo del Vicente Calderón por 30 millones de euros. Llegaba desde la Real Sociedad como un fino jugador de banda izquierda y, tras la mili de Simeone, acabó siendo uno de los mejores delanteros de Europa. Por impacto ofensivo, por influencia en el juego. Durante las últimas 12 temporadas ha jugado 10 campañas (del 14 al 19 y del 21 al 26) en el Atlético. Dos lo hizo en el Barça, que pagó 120 millones de euros de su cláusula para luego 'malvenderlo' por 40 apenas dos cursos después. Su triunfo como rojiblanco, eso sí, fue fracaso de azulgrana, club en el que nunca llegó a adaptarse. Así, este Atlético-Barça tendrá la ausencia del Principito por primera vez desde 2014. Un mundo en el que el que fuera 7 rojiblanco dibujó varias de sus mejores actuaciones (firmó ante los azulgrana cinco goles vestido de rojiblanco, ocho contando su etapa en la Real Sociedad). Inolvidable, por ahí, su exhibición en el 4-0 de las semifinales de Copa del curso pasado en un Metropolitano que, cuando suene el silbato, echará en falta a uno de los grandes genios con el balón en los píes.

articles.title: 'Eau' de Mourinho
articles.standfirst: El portugués ha creado una máquina que desprende un aroma inconfundible: "Este equipo huele bien"
articles.summary: El portugués ha creado una máquina que desprende un aroma inconfundible: "Este equipo huele bien"
articles.body: Hay perfumes que dejan huella. Y el Madrid de Mourinho empieza a tener una fragancia inconfundible. Eau de Mourinho. Una esencia que combina intensidad, carácter, compromiso y una ambición que se contagia a todo el equipo. Los números y, sobre todo, las sensaciones sobre el césped respaldan el cambio. Ocho partidos, ocho victorias y 24 goles a favor. Tres porterías a cero y tres tantos por encuentro de media. El Real Madrid se ha convertido en una máquina más contundente y fiable. Ataca con una facilidad que impresiona, pero también ha empezado a encontrar el equilibrio que tanto perseguía su entrenador. Porque la transformación no está únicamente delante. Mourinho ha conseguido algo que parecía imposible: que el Madrid no dependa exclusivamente de los destellos individuales de sus estrellas. Talento hay de sobra, pero ahora hay una estructura colectiva que lo sostiene. Trabajan todos, corren todos, presionan todos y defienden todos. Hay solidaridad, compromiso, intensidad y una implicación que hacía tiempo que no se veía. Las individualidades marcan diferencias, pero el equipo ya no vive de ellas. Una mordida que llevaba tiempo sin verse. En Mestalla llegó el broche perfecto. Octava victoria consecutiva para cerrar un pleno de parón a parón y meter presión a los protagonistas del partido del Metropolitano. El entrenador destacó la concentración de sus futbolistas y la importancia de sumar los tres puntos: "El modo fantástico en el que cada jugador ha entrado concentrado, consciente de la dificultad del partido. Con el partido de mañana, era muy importante ganar hoy, porque mañana ganamos puntos a uno de los dos o a los dos". En Mestalla encontró lo que buscaba: "Después del AEK dije que ganar en el último partido con remontada es un feeling fantástico, pero significa que no has hecho el partido perfecto. Y hoy el partido es perfecto". También puso en valor el desgaste acumulado durante una exigente serie de tres encuentros lejos del Bernabéu: "Esta serie de tres partidos fuera, difíciles, sin tiempo para dormir ni entrenar... Ganar estos tres partidos y, en este, que es el último de la serie, hacer este partido, es de mucho mérito de estos chicos". Y entonces llegó la frase que mejor resume el aroma que desprende este vestuario. "Desde mi experiencia, este equipo huele bien", aseguró Mourinho en rueda de prensa. Una declaración que encaja perfectamente con lo que está transmitiendo el equipo. El portugués percibe algo especial en el grupo y los resultados empiezan a darle la razón. Eau de Mourinho, una fórmula que funciona y que cada jornada parece más consolidada.
