articles.title: Rafa Nadal no debe ser el mando a distancia de nadie
articles.summary: Una opinión de Pedro Morata
articles.body: He conocido muchos presidentes que cuando se van, no se quieren ir de verdad y quieren seguir mandando desde su casa. No sé si es el caso de Florentino; pero estoy seguro de que eso lo llevará en la cabeza porque por su edad es lógico que vaya pensando que su presidencia tiene una fecha de caducidad más cercana que lejana. Recuerdo un caso que viví en primera persona. Año 1997 en Valencia. Paco Roig (hermano del dueño de Mercadona Juan Roig ) era un presidente muy populista y durante un par de años fue el ídolo del valencianismo. Hasta que sus formas se llevaron por delante su presidencia a los 3 años. Dimitió, pero no quiso irse del todo. Dentro del club, por consejo de su hermano, había entrado a trabajar Manuel Llorente, ex director general de Mercadona. Creo que se lo aconsejaron porque Paco era un poco descuidado con las cuentas, los números y el dinero y Paco aceptó. Pero cuando dimitió, quería seguir mandando desde su casa con el mando a distancia de Llorente. Jamás lo consiguió, afortunadamente para el Valencia CF. ¿Y qué pinta Rafa Nadal en esto? Pues puede ser que nada… o mucho; pero como yo le otorgo a Florentino el beneficio de la duda, de que todavía no da puntada sin hilo, estoy seguro de que el nombramiento de Rafa Nadal como nuevo directivo del Real Madrid tiene algo más detrás que el simple hecho de ser directivo en el Madrid, que es poco o nada, porque todos sabemos que, en las votaciones (cuando las hay) simplemente inclinan la cabeza a la decisión que ya ha tomado Florentino. Más allá de sentarse en el palco y tener ventajas de entradas (que ya es mucho) ser directivo del Real Madrid es un título honorífico o decorativo. Lo que no sé es si Florentino le ha explicado a Nadal lo que lleva en su cabeza el presidente. No hay duda de que Florentino es Florentino y con este movimiento nos lo recuerda. Y lo que no hay duda tampoco es que tiene dos tormentos que le invaden: 1.- ¿Cómo salir del lío que ha anunciado de privatizar parte del Real Madrid vistiéndolo de donación a los socios? De momento ni lo lleva como prometió a la próxima Asamblea, señal de que se le está haciendo bola y que no encuentra como hacer cuadrado el círculo. 2.- ¿Cómo seguir mandando en el club, a través de su ahijado Anas Laghrari, cuando ya no presida el club..? Esas dos cosas cuando llegue el momento no las tapa ni las maquilla con hacer directivo a Nadal ni a Fernando Alonso ni sacerdote oficial del club al Papa León XIV, todos ellos reconocidos madridistas. No conozco personalmente a Rafa como para opinar sobre su forma de ser y su personalidad. Así a primera vista, cuando me enteré de que iba a ser directivo del Real Madrid, mi primera reacción fue "¿Para qué se mete Rafa Nadal en este berenjenal?". Si es por ir al palco o tener buen sitio en las finales, realmente Rafa no lo necesita. Su figura es tan grande que sólo llamando al presidente tiene siempre acceso al palco, y a lo que necesite, y con más motivo habiéndose manifestado en público como seguidor madridista. Rafa vive en Mallorca, muy tranquilo y no creo que esté en su cabeza tener el compromiso de viajar todos los partidos o una gran mayoría a ver al Real Madrid en Madrid o donde juegue. Estará cansado de viajes de toda una vida sin bajarse del avión por el tenis. Ser directivo del Real Madrid tampoco te da un estatus que mole tanto. A los directivos del Madrid apenas se les conoce y Rafa no lo necesita. Es más conocido Rafa que Florentino en el mundo. Por tanto, por ego no es. ¿Entonces por qué da este paso? Desde el punto de vista de Rafa no lo acabo de entender porque además es un paso que le puede traer más incomodidades que ventajas. Luego me explicaré sobre eso. Pero ¿y Florentino? ¿Por qué da este paso? Yo tengo una opinión al respecto. Cuando se vaya no se querrá ir del todo. Florentino tenía y tiene una aspiración que sabe que no tiene encaje ni a martillazos. Como escribí aquí en noviembre de 2024, su idea es que su “ahijado” Anas Laghrari fuese su heredero. Pero Florentino sabe que Anas no podrá ser presidente y que podría controlar el club desde fuera pero con Anas desde dentro. Con Anas y con su amigo Bernd Reichart (el gestor de negocio que fichó Florentino con la recomendación de Anas) para promover la (fallida) SuperLiga. Anas Laghrari y Bernd Reichart no podrían ganar unas elecciones en el Real Madrid aunque les apoyara Florentino desde fuera o le dejara el dinero del aval a Anas para poderse presentar (desconozco si tiene 20 años de antigüedad). El presidente del Real Madrid teme y no quiere que el próximo presidente sea Enrique Riquelme y sabe que hay muchas posibilidades porque ha sido el propio Florentino el que indirectamente lo ha promocionado y lo ha puesto en el mapa. Ese 35% de votos que sacó Riquelme es un indicador claro. Dejó buena imagen, demostró que puede poner el aval y que no es ningún cantamañanas. Además Riquelme tendrá ahora el tiempo que no tuvo en 20 días para formarse un equipo potente a su alrededor y sobre todo para no cometer más errores de figuras que juegan a dos bandas. Un héroe de una de las Copas de Europa recientes, también jugó al sí pero no. Así que Florentino necesita un nombre bonito, una figura indiscutible, que despierte admiración, que sea madridista y que casi nadie le ponga un pero. Y ese podría ser Rafa Nadal. Su jugada ideal sería Rafa de presidente para que gane las elecciones y su ahijado Anas Laghrari como verdadero presidente con otro nombre CEO, Vicepresidente Ejecutivo etc. Pero para eso se necesita que Rafa Nadal sea un mando a distancia. Es decir, que asuma que es una figura decorativa. Y ahí es donde yo no conozco a Rafa para saber si él ha aceptado o aceptaría ese papel. Diría que no porque es que Rafa no necesita hacer ese papelón…. pero no lo puedo asegurar. No entro en si cumple los requisitos o no. Le faltan 5 años para tener 20 de antigüedad y desconozco si Rafa tiene patrimonio para avalar 135 millones o si se los prestaría Florentino, con el pacto de “Rafa tu presides pero Anas manda". Luego hay otro aspecto a analizar. Que Rafa Nadal sea una leyenda como tenista no significa que sea un buen gestor para una maquina gigante como el Real Madrid. He conocido decenas de jugadores de fútbol, algunos de ellos campeones del mundo, que no valían después para ser entrenadores, aún habiéndolo querido ser. Pero eso es harina de otro costal. No obstante hasta que llegue eso, Rafa será directivo de un presidente que quiere hacer algo raro con el club: privatizar una parte. ¿Va a ser Rafa Nadal uno de los directivos que participe en eso? En algo que va a traer polémica, campañas de críticas, plataformas que se van a organizar en contra….etc. ¿Qué necesidad tiene Rafa de ser directivo de semejante controversia? Doy por sentado que ha tenido en cuenta todo esto antes de aceptar el cargo. Y aun así ha dicho que sí. Siempre puede dimitir si no le gusta el percal… pero si ves las nubes grises oscuras a lo lejos ¿para qué salir de casa? No me gustaría para nada que Rafa emborrone con algo que no necesita, su preciosa imagen de deportista del que todo español nos sentimos orgullosos. Creo que Rafa debería medir muy bien eso. Y si ha aceptado ser directivo sólo para estar por estar, la verdad es no lo entiendo. Pero Rafa es mayor de edad, tiene experiencia en una larga ristra de personas que habrán querido aprovecharse de su fama y le supongo un hombre con criterio maduro. Nadal y Enrique Riquelme Por otra parte Rafa Nadal tiene una relación de amistad y de negocios con Riquelme. La empresa de energía Grupo COX (propiedad de Riquelme) patrocina el equipo de lanchas rápidas eléctricas que tiene Nadal. Son abundantes los rastros públicos que hay de ambos, juntos, sonrientes y en gran complicidad, en el Instagram del equipo de Nadal : el @e1teamrafa. Resulta curioso visitar el perfil de Instagram y ver a Nadal con un mono de competición con el logo de COX en el pecho. Nadal el fichaje de Florentino resulta que está patrocinado por el rival de Florentino. Raro ¿no? ¿ Qué va a hacer romper el patrocinio? A Florentino no le hará gracia. Riquelme en plena campaña electoral, asistió al estreno del documental de Nadal en Netflix. No estuvo Florentino. En aquellos días, Rafa quiso desmarcarse de la lucha de poder por las elecciones y publicó un tuit aclaratorio diciendo que no iba con ninguno de los dos candidatos. “He leído informaciones que me relacionan con posibles candidaturas a la presidencia del Real Madrid. Me gustaría aclarar que dichas informaciones no son ciertas". En aquellos días se le relacionaba con Riquelme por algo que explicaré después. Riquelme no utilizó el nombre de Nadal nunca, pero se sabía la vinculación entre ambos. Como aquel tuit quedó algo frio, Nadal al día siguiente en EFE matizó “ …tengo una buena relación con Enrique, pero tengo un grandísimo respeto por Florentino y por todo lo que es. No quería alimentar una especulación de la que no participo…. Sólo quería dejar claro que no estoy en ese momento “. Está claro que en esa época Florentino y Anas Laghrari ya estaban seduciéndolo. Sin embargo días después de la campaña electoral ( 12-13 Junio) Nadal y Riquelme estaban juntos con las mujeres en Dubrovnik con la competición de las lanchas rápidas eléctricas. 6 meses después de esas declaraciones pre electorales, Rafa parece que sí está en el momento y ha aceptado ser directivo… con Florentino. Riquelme le ha deseado en su cuenta de Instagram suerte de forma tan caballerosa como sibilina "Querido Rafa, es una alegría tener a alguien como tu en el Real Madrid. Integro, leal y gran madridista. Contigo el Madrid gana y como hemos comentado en varias ocasiones , siempre, primero el Madrid. Seguro que tú nos ayudas a evitar la venta del club, a dignificar ser socio del Real Madrid y evitar irregularidades que viven miles de socios logrando mas transparencia y democracia. Estoy con ganas de invitarte a nuestra plataforma de socios y que conozcas de primera mano las inquietudes y los problemas de los socios. Ahora tu puedes hacer mucho por los socios desde dentro. Confiamos en ti". Que ahora Nadal, abruptamente, sea directivo de Florentino es sin duda un golpe de efecto de Florentino sobre Riquelme aunque el único que puede hacer directivo del Real Madrid a Rafa es quien ostenta la presidencia oficialmente. Estoy convencido de que si la ostentara Riquelme, igualmente Nadal aceptaría ser directivo, pero lo que no podría aspirar es a ser presidente porque lo será o sería Riquelme y por ello no necesitará un mando a distancia, pero estaría encantado de tenerlo como miembro destacado de la directiva. Tampoco está claro que Nadal quiera ser presidente del Madrid porque eso le obligaría a tener una vida distinta a la que tiene en Mallorca. Muy posiblemente los deseos y necesidades de Florentino y Riquelme con Nadal son distintas.

articles.title: Cray Wanderers v Stockport County: Cray set for maiden FA Cup first-round appearance
articles.summary: Cray Wanderers host Stockport County in the FA Cup first round, with 112 league places separating the two sides.
articles.body:
If at first you do not succeed, try and try again. And again. Until, at the 78th attempt, you finally make it.

Formed in 1860, Cray Wanderers are one of the oldest football clubs in the world - and the oldest club in London still in existence.

And yet the Wands had never reached the FA Cup first round in their 166-year history.

It was perhaps fitting that Cray only just scraped through in the fourth qualifying round against Bedford Town in dramatic fashion to achieve something they have tried and failed to do 77 times before.

Following a 0-0 draw on 17 October away at Bedford, it was back to Flamingo Park for a replay three days later.

The game ended 1-1 after 90 minutes and went to extra time.

Bedford then took the lead in the 101st minute, only for Cray striker Ade Yusuff - who has scored in all four rounds so far - to make it 2-2 and force a penalty shootout.

Wands goalkeeper JJ Briggs, who is on loan from Cambridge United, made two saves in the shootout to help pave the way for history to be made in Chislehurst.

When teenager Jakob Lowe stuck away his effort from 12 yards to seal a 4-3 win on penalties, the scale of the moment was not lost on club captain Frankie Raymond.

"It means a massive amount to us all," Raymond told BBC London.

"It's a club steeped in history and to be the first set of players and staff to take the club to the first round is a massive achievement for everyone."

Raymond is right about the remarkable history at Cray.

From helping to form the Kent League in 1894 and serving as a nursery club to Woolwich Arsenal - known today simply as Arsenal - between 1895 and 1907, much has gone before in this little pocket of south-east London.

And in more recent times, the Cray Wanderers youth setup is where it all started for Manchester City and England centre-back Marc Guehi at the age of six.

BBC to show Cray Wanderers v Stockport & Altrincham v Notts County

England's Marc Guehi makes me so proud - ex-coach

Cray are 18th in the Isthmian League Premier Division - the seventh tier of the English football pyramid.

Tim O'Shea's side are only outside the relegation zone on goal difference, although they do have at least four games in hand on the teams around them.

The journey to the FA Cup first round has been far from simple for the Wands, with three replays required in the four qualifying rounds, meaning they have played seven matches - with 660 minutes of football - to make their dream a reality.

And their reward for getting this far? One of the hardest draws possible at this stage of the competition.

They will host League One's second-placed team Stockport County, live on BBC Two on Sunday (14:15 GMT).

FA Cup first round: Cray Wanderers v Stockport County

School on Friday, Stockport at home on Sunday

For Cray's top goalscorer Yusuff, Friday will be spent in the school classroom where he works as a teacher before his attentions turn to the biggest game in the club's history at the weekend.

The school corridors have been full of "really excited" pupils chatting about the upcoming encounter against the Hatters, the 32-year-old said.

"They're really looking forward to it, they're really proud," Yusuff added.

Despite Stockport being 112 league positions higher than Cray, Yusuff hopes he can keep his cup goalscoring run going.

"I don't see why not," he said. "The team are in really good form and when the boys are creating chances the way they are, I always back myself - no matter who it's against - to score."

Yusuff also believes they can cause an upset, having already knocked out National League South side Maidstone United and National League North team Bedford.

"I think it's all about momentum," he said. "We've beaten higher teams in different positions in the earlier rounds. I think it's about believing in ourselves.

"A lot of the boys here have really good careers ahead of them. They have to have these occasions and these moments so they can say: 'I can do it and I can achieve something myself'."

'There's always a David and Goliath story...'

Someone else who refuses to rule out a giant-killing is Cray Wanderers fan Mark Hunt.

"Anything could happen," he said. "There's always a David and Goliath story. We had one last year when Macclesfield beat Crystal Palace.

"There's a big, big gap between Macclesfield and Palace. Why can't it be Stockport v Cray?

"Most people expect the underdogs to fail, most times they will, but a few slip through the net.

"You get one shot at it. And the fact it goes straight to a penalty shootout, no replay, no VAR, artificial pitch - it could go in our favour."

Attendances at Flamingo Park fluctuate between 130 and 900, but Sunday's tie with Stockport sold out in five minutes, with 2,500 fans expected.

"It means the world," added Hunt. "It's been such a long time coming. It's something we've been waiting for for so long, just to get a shot at a Stockport County.

"It's going to be an incredible occasion."

articles.title: Brighton tactics: How Fabian Hurzeler's 'brave' defence poses tricky puzzle to solve
articles.summary: Brighton's unique defensive shape has provided the platform for the Seagulls' superb start to the Premier League season.
articles.body:
"We have a great chance on Saturday to take revenge," were Fabian Hurzeler's words as Brighton exited the Carabao Cup at the hands of Manchester City .

The following Saturday, the 33-year-old's dogged defiance manifested in a 1-0 victory over the same opponents, who failed to score at home for the first time in 23 matches.

Brighton now sit in third place, only behind City and Premier League leaders Arsenal , both teams they have beaten this season.

And they have done so with a bravery and front-footedness that the likes of Arsenal and City have not always been used to facing.

With 24 goals in nine games, Brighton are the league's top scorers but it is their defensive work that has underpinned their underdog victories against the league's best teams.

Notably, Brighton have conceded just seven goals this season - with only Arsenal conceding fewer.

From opposition goal-kicks, Brighton look to press high and in a man-to-man fashion. This is a common approach but Brighton 's intensity across the pitch makes them better at executing this than most.

The challenge is that the opposition will have an extra player in their build-up compared to Brighton 's 10 pressing outfielders, if they use their keeper as a passing option.

That potential issue is managed by one of Brighton 's attackers leaving the centre-back they began marking - curving their run as they press the opposition keeper.

In curving their run, the aim is to cut off the passing angle back to they player they are no longer marking, while the rest of the team are responsible for their direct, individual opponents.

In spite of generally opting to play man-to-man across the pitch, at points in their build-up the team in possession may have an unmarked player.

This player is usually in an area of the pitch that is hard for them to access - such as their full-back or winger on the far side.

This is often an intentional decision Brighton take, believing the benefit of an extra pressing player closer to the ball is greater than the risk associated with leaving that opposing player unmarked.

By ensuring the opposing unmarked player is far from the ball, they reduce the likelihood that player is found. By putting more bodies around the ball, they increase the likelihood of winning the ball back.

What makes Brighton so unique though is how they defend deeper.

Most teams who press high from opposition goal-kicks then settle into a more rigid defensive shape closer to their own goal. These defensive blocks are generally examples of zonal defending rather than man-to-man defending.

The most common defensive block for top teams tends to come in the form of a 4-4-2. Players are tasked with marshalling specific 'zones', aiming to make it harder for opponents to get into dangerous positions. There is often a focus on blocking the centre of the pitch, with the wider areas less congested for opponents to play in.

Brighton 's magic this season is in the form of continuing to use man-to-man ideas, albeit in a more measured fashion, when pushed closer to their own goal.

This more measured version of a man-to-man press is seen in Brighton 's use of an extra player, or a 'plus-one' (+1) in their backline. Put simply, if opponents commit four forwards high up the pitch, Brighton will defend with five.

As such, Brighton aren't looking to go man-to-man everywhere, always, but they are looking to do it as much as they can while adhering to two key principles: trying to keep a plus-one in defence and while focusing on blocking the centre of the pitch.

These ideas were seen clearly against Manchester City too.

In possession, Enzo Maresca asked right-back Matheus Nunes to push up and move infield, into a position that resembled a right-sided striker.

City, as well as the likes of Paris St-Germain and Arsenal , have used their full-backs in these unorthodox attacking positions as it poses difficult questions to the opponent who tracks them.

These players tend to find space as opposing wingers are typically less willing to track an attacking full-back all the way into their own box.

Hurzeler has used Maxim de Cuyper as his left winger this season, but the Belgian has played the majority of his career at left-back. This has equipped him with the work-rate and defensive nous to deal with the modern, roaming attacking full-back.

In man-to-man fashion, De Cuyper followed Nunes all the way into his fixed position higher up the pitch, and ended up defending at left centre-back - as Brighton created a back five. When Brighton had the ball, De Cuyper was back playing at left wing.

Remember Brighton keeping a +1 at the back? Naturally, this leaves the other team with a spare player somewhere else. It is usually one of the opposition centre-backs who remain unmarked, finding themselves with time and space on the ball.

In an ideal situation, a centre-back less confident on the ball would be a good candidate to leave unmarked.

But even for impressive ball-playing defenders, the challenge is that every player they could pass to remains marked or could become marked in a fraction of a second based on how Brighton set-up.

Brighton are also continually shifting, looking to find moments in which one player can spring to press the unmarked centre-back on the ball. When this jump happens, Brighton will lock on to a full man-to-man press, looking to force a turnover or push the opposition back towards their keeper.

There are solutions to this organised yet man-oriented defending and Abdukodir Khusanov's powerful ball-carrying from a wider position was perhaps the best Manchester City had on show.

But combining key principles in the form of blocking the centre of the pitch and not being baited into mindlessly tracking players looking to stretch their shape, while still locking on to individual players nearby, make Brighton an incredibly difficult puzzle for teams to solve.

For as potent as they have been in attack, it is their bravery in defence that has given them the platform.

articles.title: Atlético - Barça: Tensión... y liderato
articles.standfirst: El que gane esta noche encabezará la clasificación. Se reencuentran tras el ‘culebrón’ Julián... y los seis choques del curso pasado marcados por las polémicas
articles.summary: El que gane esta noche encabezará la clasificación. Se reencuentran tras el ‘culebrón’ Julián... y los seis choques del curso pasado marcados por las polémicas
articles.body: Tensión. La provocada entre Atlético y Barça durante el maratón de duelos de la temporada pasada. Seis choques entre Liga, Copa y Champions que acabaron con declaraciones cruzadas, denuncias por arbitrajes y un subidón de tensión pocas veces visto entre los dos conjuntos. Tensión. La generada por el ‘culebrón Julián’, con el manifiesto interés azulgrana en el jugador, palabras de Laporta y el entorno culé pidiendo que se atendiera la oferta por el argentino de 100 millones de euros, respuestas contundentes de Miguel Ángel Gil sobre que jamás le vendería el jugador al Barcelona y ‘balas cruzadas’ desde ambos bandos. Tensión. La que se espera esta noche sobre el verde del Metropolitano, tanto por la figura de un Julián arrepentido como en un palco que presidirá Enrique Cerezo y que contará con la presencia de Joan Laporta, cabeza visible de un Barça que quedó expuesto públicamente por todo el asunto sobre el delantero del Atlético de Madrid. Todo ello, todo lo que rodea la atmósfera de este gran partido, no debe impedir poner en valor la dimensión del encuentro. Por la calidad de los futbolistas en el verde, por la magnitud de dos de los mejores entrenadores del mundo... y por tres puntos que valdrán un liderato. Si el Barça suma, seguirá en lo más alto. Si es el Atlético de Madrid el que se lleva los tres puntos, pondrá fin a una racha de 68 jornadas sin vivir en lo más alto. Porque desde el 12 de enero de 2025 los del Cholo no miran por encima de todos en la clasificación. Entonces le sirvió para ser campeón de invierno, ahora le valdría para dar otro golpe en la mesa (ya ganó al Madrid en el Metropolitano) y para presentar una candidatura más que fiable con su octava victoria seguida en el torneo doméstico. Pero el Barcelona también tiene el objetivo muy claro: llegar al parón ocupando el primer puesto de la clasificación. El conjunto azulgrana no quiere dejar escapar la oportunidad de consolidar su liderato. Además, nadie olvida que las dos eliminaciones sufridas la pasada temporada, tanto en la Copa como en la Champions, a manos del Atlético, siguen siendo una espina clavada en el vestuario culé. El equipo de Hansi Flick está lanzado enLaLiga y solo el Real Madrid ha logrado arrebatarle los tres puntos en este increíble arranque.Pero el potencial de los culés no se limita a los resultados. Uno de sus grandes argumentos está siendo su extraordinaria capacidad ofensiva. El bloque catalán ha conseguido marcar en todos los encuentros disputados en el campeonato regular y está exhibiendo una pegada demoledora, firmando goleadas de escándalo.

articles.title: El día de la Araña
articles.standfirst: Julián tendrá el foco del partido tras pedir su “transferencia” al Barça en verano. Buscará la redención marcando ante los azulgrana... por quinta vez
articles.summary: Julián tendrá el foco del partido tras pedir su “transferencia” al Barça en verano. Buscará la redención marcando ante los azulgrana... por quinta vez
articles.body: Transferencia. Sueño. Dos palabras que marcaron la actualidad de Atlético y Barça desde mayo a septiembre. El 25 del primero MARCA desveló en exclusiva la petición que iba a marcar el pasado verano: Julián le había comunicado a los dirigentes rojiblancos que tenía un anhelo: jugar en el Camp Nou como local. La férrea postura rojiblanca hizo saltar por los aires la voluntad de una Araña que se veía obligado a seguir en un Metropolitano que dictó sentencia con él ante el Villarreal. La música de viento recibida aquel día hizo tambalear al propio jugador, que todavía seguía teniendo un entorno que le hacía ver que era posible lo imposible: coger el puente aéreo. Pero el billete jamás tuvo opciones de ser emitido y esta noche se medirá contra su pasado más doloroso por primera vez. Hay un Atleti-Barça y Julián lo vivirá de rojiblanco mientras el ruido en su contra va decayendo gracias a sus goles (lleva dos) y al perdón que pidió tras el triunfo ante el Deportivo, en el único gol marcado hasta ahora en el Metropolitano. Por todo esto, el protagonista del choque de esta noche será Julián. Por lo que pudo ser y no fue. Porque un gol suyo con una celebración sentida puede completar el camino de la redención que todos en el Atlético necesitan. Porque todo lo vivido no cambia el paso: sin Griezmann, nadie tiene más talento entre los de Simeone que Julián, la estrella venida del Manchester City para liderar hacia los títulos a los madrileños. No es el Barça un rival que se le dé precisamente mal al 19. En el histórico 4-0 del curso pasado, más allá del recital de Griezmann, Julián marcó un gol y asistió en otro. Fue clave en un resultado que, pese al intento de remontada, le valió al Atlético para jugar la final de Copa ante la Real Sociedad. También fue clave al marcarle en la Champions, entonces en el Camp Nou, en el 0-2 con un golazo de falta que puso la primera piedra de otro pase rojiblanco ante el conjunto de Flick. En su primera temporada, la 24-25, también le marcó en Copa en el 4-4 de la Ciudad Condal. Aquella eliminatoria cayó del lado azulgrana como también el choque en LaLiga en el Metropolitano. El 19 marcó, pero el Barça remontó y acabó ganando 2-4 en el único choque en el torneo de la regularidad con picotazo de un Julián que sabe que hoy es su día, el día de la Araña.

articles.title: Del "esta entrevista es una mierda" al "no quiero que se entere el equipo contrario": ¿por qué los clubes permiten que se televise todo?
articles.standfirst: El reglamento audiovisual de LaLiga fija unos mínimos de obligado cumplimiento y, desde 2023, reparte un porcentaje del dinero televisivo según lo que cada club colabore con las cámaras
articles.summary: El reglamento audiovisual de LaLiga fija unos mínimos de obligado cumplimiento y, desde 2023, reparte un porcentaje del dinero televisivo según lo que cada club colabore con las cámaras
articles.body: Pablo Maffeo atendió a DAZN al descanso del Valencia-Real Madrid de este sábado en Mestalla, con 0-2 en el marcador, y no ocultó su enfado. "No me apetece nada hacer esta entrevista, creo que es una mierda, no pinta nada aquí", dijo el lateral valencianista, que se quejó de las decisiones del árbitro. Finalmente, terminó aceptando responder a las preguntas y, después del partido, se disculpó con el periodista al que le tocaba llevar el micrófono en ese momento. No ha sido el primer episodio de la temporada en el que uno de los protagonistas de un partido reacciona de mala manera ante la presencia de las cámaras en su entorno de trabajo. En la jornada 5, en el Sánchez-Pizjuán, el técnico del Sevilla, Luis García Plaza se encaró con el micrófono de DAZN cuando en la pausa de hidratación la pértiga se acercó al banquillo del Sevilla. El técnico lo explicó después del partido: "¡Es que no quiero que se entere el equipo contrario de lo que voy a decir, ya está, solo eso!". Semanas después explicó en COPE que, cuando el Sevilla juega, en casa el micrófono entra en su banquillo en la segunda parte; pero ese día el Valencia dijo a última hora que no entraba y a él no se lo comunicaron. García Plaza reconoció además que los entrenadores no se comportan igual cuando tienen el micrófono delante y que tiene a un colaborador pendiente de la charla del banquillo rival en cada pausa de hidratación. Estas situaciones se explican por el Reglamento para la Retransmisión Televisiva de LaLiga, en vigor en Primera División desde la temporada 2016-17 e incorporado al Reglamento General de la competición. Su base legal es el Real Decreto-ley 5/2015, que centralizó la venta de los derechos audiovisuales del fútbol y atribuye al Órgano de Control de LaLiga la competencia para "establecer el patrón para la producción y realización" de las retransmisiones. El propio texto establece que sus normas son "de obligado cumplimiento", salvo las que figuran como recomendaciones, y cuyo incumplimiento conlleva sanciones económicas. En cada encuentro, dos directores de Partido nombrados por LaLiga revisan una lista de comprobación. Cada infracción suma puntos negativos, que al final de la temporada se convierten en una cantidad que el club tiene que pagar. El reglamento distingue entre lo obligatorio y lo voluntario. Son obligatorias, entre otras cosas, la entrevista al entrenador antes del partido, las entrevistas "flash" y "superflash" al terminar, las ruedas de prensa y el acceso de las cámaras de LaLiga al túnel y a los banquillos. Sobre el descanso, la norma permite a las televisiones con derechos pedir entrevistas dentro del plan de producción, y si LaLiga las aprueba, el club "deberá colaborar en su realización". En cambio, la grabación de la charla técnica en el vestuario es facultativa. LaLiga solo pide a los clubes "el mejor esfuerzo" para facilitarla. El caso más reciente de un club que no cumplió es el del Athletic. A finales de agosto, después del partido en el Camp Nou, la plantilla rojiblanca se negó a hablar con los medios en protesta por la decisión de la directiva de retirar las invitaciones que recibían los futbolistas para los partidos en San Mamés. No atendieron ni a las televisiones con derechos, ni a las que les hace el propio club. Días después, algunos medios informaron de que LaLiga sancionaría al club, ya que las entrevistas ante los medios de comunicación son de obligado cumplimiento en el reglamento audiovisual. ¿Cómo se aplica la sanción? Restando puntos en la ejecución del plan de medios en lo que club recibe de variable por derechos audiovisuales. Desde 2023, el dinero 'anima' a los clubes a cumplir más allá de los mínimos obligatorios. La Junta de Primera División aprobó en agosto de aquel año, con 18 votos a favor, 2 abstenciones y un voto en contra, el del Real Madrid, un cambio en el reparto de los ingresos televisivos. Esta modificación afecta al bloque de "implantación social", que supone un 25 % del total. La mitad de los dos tercios de este porcentaje se distribuye en función del grado de colaboración en las nuevas acciones voluntarias que se plantean atendiendo a las peticiones de los broadcasters. Esa colaboración se pondera además por la audiencia de cada club. Según LaLiga, el objetivo era conseguir "una mayor disposición" de los clubes para facilitar entrevistas a entrenadores y cuerpo técnico, grabaciones de las arengas en el vestuario o una mayor participación de los jugadores. Se calculó entonces que el fondo rondaría los 130 millones de euros, repartidos según un sistema de puntos de 175 a 500. El mínimo se cumplía con las entrevistas flash y la producción habitual. La cifra cambia cada temporada, porque el fondo es un porcentaje de lo que se reparte. Como referencia, en la temporada 2024-2025 los 42 clubes se repartieron 1.432 millones de euros por derechos televisivos. Y lo que está en juego seguirá creciendo: LaLiga prevé superar los 6.135 millones de euros en ingresos audiovisuales domésticos en el ciclo 2027/28–2031/32, un 9 % más que el periodo anterior, con DAZN y Movistar Plus+ como operadores. La tendencia no es solo española. Después de un Mundial en el que las pausas de hidratación fueron obligatorias en todos los partidos -aunque más con fines publicitarios- la Conmebol ha llevado esa práctica a la Copa Libertadores. En su manual para los clubes, durante esas pausas "se permitirá la aproximación de cámaras y micrófonos específicos" de la Conmebol a los banquillos de cada equipo. En España, la decisión de abrir o no esos espacios sigue recayendo en parte en cada club. Pero desde 2023 tiene un coste: menos puntos en el reparto y, por tanto, menos dinero para los clubes.

articles.summary: Es el rival que más goles le ha marcado
articles.body: Mejorar los registros defensivos es uno de los hándicaps del Barcelona y una de las preocupaciones de Hansi Flick. Alabado y reconocido por su capacidad ofensiva, suma ¡46! goles a favor en LaLiga, el Barça ha mostrado cierta fragilidad en su retaguardia, tanto en el torneo doméstico como en la Champions League, a pesar de contar con uno de los porteros más destacados del panorama mundial: Joan García. El meta catalán se mide, precisamente, esta noche a su peor rival: el Atlético de Madrid es el contrincante que más tantos le ha marcado en su carrera, 10, y al que más veces se ha medido: 8. El Barcelona logró el pasado martes, en la Champions League, dejar su portería a cero después de ¡18! encuentros en Europa sin lograrlo. Joan García y todo el bloque culé impidieron que el Aston Villa superara su meta, y acabar imbatidos fue celebrado por los culés como una gran gesta. Los catalanes confían ahora en extender a LaLiga ese logro. El Barça ha recibido 12 goles en la competición doméstica, 10 los ha encajado Joan García (se perdió la segunda mitad del partido contra el Racing y el del Sevilla por una lesión en la rodilla), y encadena tres sin dejar su portería a cero, desde el compromiso contra el Getafe. Estas cifras no acaban de satisfacer a Flick, que exige un mejor rendimiento y un mayor sacrificio, a todos sus hombres, atrás. El Atlético, por ejemplo, tiene mejores registros: sólo ha recibido ocho tantos en las 11 jornadas disputadas. El bloque del Metropolitano es, de hecho, el menos goleado de la competición. Pero también se están mostrando más competitivos en defensa que el Barcelona el Real Madrid, el Athletic y el Celta, en estas primeras 11 jornadas. Joan García se reencuentra esta noche con el Atlético, que es el equipo al que más veces se ha medido en su carrera. Ha disputado ocho partidos (entre LaLiga, la Champions League y la Copa del Rey) contra los de Simeone, seis con la camiseta azulgrana (dos en cada torneo) y dos con la del Espanyol. En estos cruces, ha encajado 10 goles, 9 como culé. Con el Barcelona, su balance es de cuatro victorias y dos derrotas, y sólo en un choque resultó imbatido: fue en el compromiso de la segunda vuelta de las semifinales de la Copa del Rey de la temporada pasada. En el resto de cruces, encajó dianas. El marcador más abultado fue en la ida de la competición del K.O: el Barça cayó por un doloroso 4-0 en el Metropolitano. Joan García confía esta noche en sumar su segundo encuentro como azulgrana imbatido contra el Atlético de Madrid y alargar a LaLiga su buen hacer demostrado en la Champions League, donde el pasado martes el Barça cerró su arco por primera vez tras 18 partidos. En sus dos partidos contra el Atlético en LaLiga, de la temporada pasada, siempre logró la victoria, pero no consiguió dejar su portería a cero. Esta noche, para alcanzar su objetivo deberá estar especialmente atento a Álex Baena, que es el máximo realizador rojiblanco con cinco goles.

articles.title: Lionel Messi makes history with consecutive MLS Golden Boot wins
articles.summary: Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi becomes the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons.
articles.body:
Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge.

Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips.

In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row.

And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner.

The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup.

Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville.

They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.

articles.title: Messi gana su segunda Bota de Oro de la MLS
articles.standfirst: El argentino ganó su segundo trofeo goleador de la MLS de manera consecutiva tras terminar la temporada regular con 26 goles
articles.summary: El argentino ganó su segundo trofeo goleador de la MLS de manera consecutiva tras terminar la temporada regular con 26 goles
articles.body: La MLS disputó este sábado su trigésima cuarta y última jornada de la temporada regular, en la que quedaron definidos los 'playoffs', que arrancarán el próximo 19 de noviembre. El Inter Miami, que terminó el campeonato segundo en el Este, dejó escapar un 3-0 (Ian Fray, Luis Suárez y Rodrigo de Paul) en la primera mitad para terminar empatando 3-3 frente al Charlotte. Messi no vio portería en el Nu Stadium de Miami, pero aún así se aseguró la Bota de Oro por segundo año consecutivo con 26 goles. Segundo quedó el croata Petar Musa, del Dallas, con 22, seguido de Surridge (21). El Inter Miami se enfrentará en primera ronda de los 'playoff' al Columbus Crew, que logró la última plaza de la fase final tras derrotar 3-4 al Chicago Fire con un gol del gallego Brais Méndez en el minuto 93. El Nashville, campeón de la Supporters' Shield, terminó líder de la Conferencia Este con 77 puntos, que superan el récord del Inter Miami de 2024 con 74. En el Oeste, quedaron primeros los Vancouver Whitecaps. El Nashville derrotó en esta última jornada por 0-2 al Cincinnati con doblete del delantero inglés Sam Surridge, mientras el Vancouver obtuvo idéntico resultado en Montreal con tantos del senegalés Cheikh Sabaly y del moldavo Mihail Gherasimencov. Segundo en el Oeste terminó el Dallas, que este sábado se impuso por 3-1 al Colorado con goles del uruguayo Joaquín Valiente, el brasileño Kaick y el colombiano Santiago Moreno. En otros partidos de la última jornada, el Orlando City de Antoine Griezmann ganó por 1-0 al New England Revolution con gol del paraguayo Braian Ojeda y disputará la repesca contra el Cincinnati, de donde saldrá el rival del Nashville en primera ronda. El Real Salt Lake ganó y eliminó al Los Angeles Galaxy por 2-1 con un gol del catalán Sergi Solans, decimoquinto que marca esta temporada. El equipo de Utah disputará la repesca del Oeste contra el Seattle Sounders, que también ganó por 2-1 al LAFC.

articles.title: Mohamed Salah and life in Turkey after leaving Liverpool for Trabzonspor
articles.summary: BBC Sport travels to Turkey to watch Mohamed Salah play for Trabzonspor and discover how the 'Egyptian King' is settling into life by the Black Sea.
articles.body:
Back in August, when Mohamed Salah landed in Istanbul after flying in from his holiday in Mykonos, he wore Trabzonspor's burgundy and blue home strip as he stepped out of the plane to be greeted by thousands of fans.

That kit sold out almost instantly. Later that day, as Salah headed to Trabzon in north-east Turkey to complete the formalities of one of the most unexpected transfers, he asked one of his entourage what he should wear.

"The same kit," came the response, but Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan advised Salah to wear the black away kit instead. Of course, that sold out too.

From the outset of the 34-year-old's arrival to this historic port city on the Black Sea, that sense of adulation has only grown.

"I went to the airport to see him in Istanbul and it was surreal," says Nisa Dumangoz. "I still can't believe that he is one of us."

Go for a stroll through Trabzon on matchday and it is Salah's face which adorns everything. Even the walls inside the fishmongers have pictures of him.

At the club shop in town, one of the staff jokes that the ground floor is for the Egyptian and the upper floor is for everything else.

Outside the stadium, there are scarves, magnets, keyrings, lighters with his face on and Egyptian Nemes headdresses in Trabzonspor colours. Season ticket sales rocketed after his arrival.

"Walking around Trabzon, it feels as though nine out of every 10 fans wearing a shirt have Salah's name on the back. The 10th has their own," says Turkish football journalist Hasan Tuncel.

The club have surpassed their merchandise revenue from last year in three months since Salah's arrival, while the local airport is only getting busier.

Liverpool was difficult to reach for many supporters across the Arab world and tickets were often hard to source. Trabzon is far more accessible, with new flights introduced from Cairo, Dubai and Riyadh since Salah's arrival.

On our flight from Istanbul, we meet an Egyptian family of 10 coming from Cairo for Trabzonspor's Uefa Conference League game against Freiburg.

"He is our ambassador and our Egyptian King, and with how many people want to come to Turkey now, he is their ambassador too," says Mahmoud.

At the game, there is a group of Egyptian celebrities and influencers. A quick check of their social media shows their combined Instagram following of about five million. Trabzonspor have three million. Salah has 68 million.

Salah recently went for a hike and posed for a picture on a rock in the Trabzon highlands. That rock has been renamed Salahtasi (Salah's Rock) and is now a tourist destination.

The commercial element of his signing has more than been justified but crucially, on the pitch, Salah is driving Trabzonspor's push for the Turkish Super Lig title and he has hit the ground running with 10 goals and five assists in all competitions.

Trabzonspor trail leaders Galatasaray by three points, having won seven of their first 10 games, including victories against the table-toppers and Besiktas.

For context, the Istanbul 'big three' of Galatasaray (26), Fenerbahce (19) and Besiktas (16) have won the league on 61 occasions combined, compared with Trabzonspor's seven titles.

"In Turkey, he is the biggest football star after Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo," says Kerim Tonyali, who is part of Gurbetci Gencler, a Trabzonspor supporters' group.

And given Salah's status as an icon, Trabzonspor are quickly becoming the second club for many in Turkey and the wider Muslim world.

Determined to prove he still has what it takes

Trabzon may be more than 2,000 miles from Liverpool but there are similarities, particularly when it comes to the sense of identity and pride associated with originating from here.

"Everywhere is Trabzon for us," is the local mantra and aligns with the sense of unity within this city that has a population of about 800,000 and is only the 30th-biggest in Turkey.

For Salah, the financials were important and he is earning about £14.6m per year as well as 20% of official merchandise sold with his name on, but one of the key aspects of coming here was the ability to focus entirely on his football.

Besiktas was considered as an option after the 2026 World Cup but, after multiple calls with Trabzonspor, Salah felt they were the ideal fit and offered a life away from the hustle and bustle of Istanbul.

He has his own security detail and is living in the nearby town of Yomra, where he now has a street named after him. He also employs a private chef and, unsurprisingly, continues to set standards in the gym and on the training ground.

By all accounts, Salah is thriving. He is a fan of Turkish coffee and is often spotted leaving the ground with Ayran - a traditional yogurt drink - but as much as he wants to explore the city, he knows of the difficulties given his reputation.

"Everyone wants to work with a star like Mohamed Salah," said Trabzonspor's Paul Onuachu, formerly of Southampton. "He adds so much and helps all of us and he contributes positively. I am grateful for him. It's a blessing to play with him."

Watching Salah in the flesh in a Conference League game against Freiburg, his pace has gone down a notch compared with his peak but the touch, quick feet and sheer quality is still there. And so is that knack of getting in goalscoring positions, even if his defensive duties - which were such a source of debate last season at Liverpool - are limited.

Salah believes he still has plenty to give for club and country, with aspirations to play in both the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations and 2030 World Cup, which will be partly held in North Africa.

No decision has been made about how long he will stay in Turkey, but there is growing belief among sources in the Middle East that he will move to Saudi Arabia when his two-year Trabzonspor deal expires in 2028. By then, he will be 36.

'The thing in life that has brought me the most joy'

On initial thoughts, it is easy to question how and why Salah ended up here.

When he delivered that infamous mixed-zone interview at Leeds ' Elland Road less than a year ago and the wheels of his departure from Liverpool were set in motion, surely no-one would have imagined his next destination would be this Turkish outpost near the Georgian border.

"I remember looking at him when we landed in Trabzon and seeing the crowds outside and how emotional it was," says Anil Dincer, one of the lawyers involved in Salah's move to Turkey.

"We already have Salah and Fabinho. So now we are waiting for [Virgil] Van Dijk," adds Serhat Sumer, a Trabzonspor fan.

Salah, of course, delivered so much joy to Liverpool and the intention here is the same. This is no drift towards retirement, but a player determined to prove he still belongs at the highest level and that football still has meaning beyond trophies and money.

Asked by BBC Sport if he had a message for Liverpool fans, Salah simply said "hello" and smiled. Given how rarely he spoke in the mixed zone during his time at Anfield, it is not in his nature to talk regularly on record.

Last season was Salah's least prolific at Anfield, but given Liverpool 's struggles in front of goal in the Premier League, it is hard to argue they have replaced one of their greatest ever players.

Perhaps a time will come when the likes of Salah, Arne Slot and Richard Hughes will reveal more about the chain of events that led to the forward agreeing to terminate his contract a year early. As it is, none of them are at the club and that chapter is firmly closed.

Salah's influence that once helped shape the Premier League is now being felt on the shores of the Black Sea. He is Trabzonspor's force of nature. And the team known as the Black Sea Storm are rising and on the hunt for silverware with their Egyptian King.

articles.title: Bernardo Silva hails Real Madrid dominance as red-hot Blancos extend winning streak with Valencia demolition
articles.summary: Bernardo Silva has praised Real Madrid's defensive solidity after a commanding 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla. The Portuguese star believes their eigh...
articles.body:
Bernardo Silva has praised Real Madrid's defensive solidity after a commanding 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla. The Portuguese star believes their eighth consecutive win puts the club in a prime position to challenge for both Liga and Champions League glory this season.

Silva played a starring role as Madrid cruised to a 3-0 victory against Valencia at Mestalla. The Portuguese midfielder featured for 84 minutes during an excellent individual display in the heart of the pitch.

The impressive away result marked an eighth consecutive win across all competitions for the Spanish club. Jose Mourinho's side currently sits in second place in the Liga standings with 30 points - level with league leaders Barcelona, ​​who are set to play their 12th match of the campaign against Atletico Madrid.

Silva highlights aggressive Valencia approach

The match was not without its challenges for the visiting side. Silva noted the physical nature of their opponents and the lenient officiating that allowed the game to flow freely.

"A tough match, in a challenging atmosphere, against an aggressive team and a referee who allowed them to be aggressive," Silva explained on the club's official website . "That made it complicated for us. Fede's [Valverde] stunning goal helped us control the game. I felt we always had control of the match and were very organized, managing their transitions very well. The defenders were very aggressive and won quick balls. We're very happy to secure three more points.

"Having eight consecutive wins puts us in a much better position to fight for La Liga and be among the top eight in the Champions League. We're very happy with this streak, but now we need to focus on the next match and keep going because the atmosphere in the dressing room and at the club is very good. We want to keep winning and winning."

Los Blancos have now recorded eight consecutive victories across all competitions. The last time they failed to secure a win was during the Madrid Derby against Atletico in late September. Silva emphasized that this achievement is crucial for his team if they wish to remain in contention for the title this season.

"It's very important because the teams that defend best are always ready to win matches and titles," he added. "That puts us closer to winning games and championships."

Club football now pauses for the international break. Silva will immediately shift his focus to international duty and travel to join his Portugal team-mates. Portugal are preparing for two important UEFA Nations League fixtures in the coming days. They will face Denmark on November 14 before concluding the international window against Wales on November 17.

Football offers no respite this November 8, 2026. After Real Madrid's commanding display at Mestalla, all eyes today turn to the decisive battle for top spot between Atlético de Madrid and FC Barcelona, while the football world celebrates Boca Juniors' title triumph and another historic record for Leo Messi.

José Mourinho's Real Madrid steamrolled their opponents at Mestalla with an emphatic win powered by goals from Fede Valverde, Arda Güler and Kylian Mbappé. Top-of-the-table showdown at the Metropolitano

The excitement continues: FC Barcelona visit Atlético de Madrid this afternoon with top spot at stake. Hansi Flick's side are defending a slender two-point lead. Eric García returns to the squad as Barça look to shatter the aura of invincibility surrounding Atlético's home ground just before the international break.

Boca reach seventh heaven at La Bombonera

In Argentina, wild celebrations erupted in the closing minutes. A dramatic late goal from Enner Valencia against Defensa y Justicia sealed a 1-0 victory and crowned Boca Juniors champions of the league's annual standings. The Xeneizes will now face Independiente Rivadavia in the round of 16.

Leo Messi continues to rewrite history in the United States. The Argentine star was officially crowned the MLS Golden Boot winner, becoming the first player ever to win the award in consecutive seasons in the US league.

Odegaard strengthens Arsenal's grip on top spot

In the Premier League, Arsenal strengthened their lead with a hard-fought 1-0 win over a battling Hull City. Martin Odegaard broke the deadlock in the 72nd minute, in a match where Mikel Arteta freshened up midfield with Mikel Merino and Martín Zubimendi.

articles.title: Skip Bayless drops ‘refund’ claim after Alabama takes down Lane Kiffin’s LSU
articles.summary: No. 14 LSU suffered a 31-13 home loss to No. 5 Alabama on Saturday at Tiger Stadium, dropping to 6-3 overall and 3-3 in SEC play. Following the defeat, popul...
articles.body:
No. 14 LSU suffered a 31-13 home loss to No. 5 Alabama on Saturday at Tiger Stadium, dropping to 6-3 overall and 3-3 in SEC play. Following the defeat, popular sports analyst Skip Bayless took to social media with a pointed remark about Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin's seven-year, $91 million contract.

"LSU is going to want a refund," he wrote on X (formerly Twitter).

The result brought another setback for Kiffin, who arrived in Baton Rouge after leaving Ole Miss. The Tigers entered the contest with expectations of competing for a national championship, but their third defeat of the season has left their College Football Playoff hopes in serious jeopardy. LSU's chances of reaching the postseason dropped from 51% to 25% after Saturday's loss, according to the Allstate Playoff Predictor.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

While the Tigers outgained the Crimson Tide 457-285, they repeatedly came up empty when it mattered the most. Quarterback Sam Leavitt completed 35 of 47 passes for 380 yards but failed to throw a touchdown and was intercepted once. He also took four sacks. Running back Jackson Harris contributed 166 receiving yards on 11 catches, while tight end Trey'Dez Green added 10 receptions for 85 yards.

However, LSU's inability to finish drives came back to ultimately haunt the team. The Tigers converted none of their four fourth-down attempts, resulting in the most fourth-down failures of Kiffin's coaching career. LSU also reached the red zone four times but managed only one touchdown and one field goal. Moreover, the Tigers missed a 56-yard field goal attempt.

LSU moved ahead 13-10 late in the third quarter through Dilin Jones' five-yard touchdown run, but that advantage lasted less than three minutes before the Crimson Tide responded with a touchdown pass from quarterback Keelon Russell to tight end Josh Ford.

Alabama then added two more touchdowns to complete a 21-point unanswered run. Russell finished with 206 passing yards and three touchdowns on 17-of-24 passing. Ryan Coleman-Williams also played a major role, returning a punt 32 yards to set up the Crimson Tide's fourth-quarter touchdown drive.

The defeat extended the Tigers' disappointing run against Alabama. LSU has now lost four consecutive meetings to the Crimson Tide, all by double-digit margins, and seven of their last eight games against them at home. Kiffin also remains winless versus Alabama as a head coach , falling to 0-6 in his career against the program.

Speaking after the game, Kiffin described the performance as "really disappointing" and acknowledged that the offensive production should have resulted in considerably more points. He also admitted he did not expect his team to be 6-3 at this stage of the season.

The Tigers now face another big challenge, with a home game against a top-10 Texas team scheduled for next week. LSU will need to win its remaining games and receive considerable help elsewhere to have a realistic opportunity to reach the College Football Playoff.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho talks Tebas, fatigue, international break, Mestalla after Valencia 0-3 Real Madrid
articles.summary: Real Madrid kept up their winning run, and have now strung together eight consecutive victories in all competitions, as they faced Valencia at Mestalla and e...
articles.body:
Real Madrid kept up their winning run, and have now strung together eight consecutive victories in all competitions, as they faced Valencia at Mestalla and emerged winners with a 3-0 scoreline. Goals from Federico Valverde, Arda Guler, and Kylian Mbappe got the Merengues the full three points, even though the hosts' physical approach to the game did not make it an easy game for the visitors.

As Diario AS has reported, Jose Mourinho talked to the press after the game. He analyzed his team's win and commented on the performances of some players.

The Portuguese coach did not appear too happy with how La Liga scheduled his team's matches:

"A message to La Liga and Tebas… I have to be humble because they have the power. I ask them not to do the same thing to us. Because it's… I don't want to say it's superhuman, because it's possible, but it's very difficult. And… if they want to play this joke, they can play it on someone else. Let us have a break after this marathon of travelling and matches, from Sunday to Saturday, which has been… which has been too much.

Do you want to know what worries me now? It worries me because… if they stayed here with me and my staff, we would give them very special attention when it comes to… to helping those players recover. But they're going away with their national teams. And with the national teams… I can imagine, although I've never coached a national team, that their coaches want to work.

And these players cannot work right now. They need to rest so that they can then play for their national teams. A little later… on Thursday, Friday or around then. But these players need a great deal of attention during their recovery process."

With the win against Valencia, Mourinho became the coach with the best winning percentage in La Liga. While expressing his pride in this, the Real Madrid coach was only looking forward to getting even more wins:

"It tells me that we have to win the next one. Because… in life, even with good numbers, numbers that mean something, people eventually forget. We don't feed off numbers from the past; we feed off the present. And we have to win the next match.

But I had no idea about that statistic. Obviously, it's a source of pride, because Spanish football has had so many top managers throughout its history. To be among them with those numbers is an honour. But, as I said, the next match is the most important thing."

The Portuguese tactician did not want any credit for the improvements shown by his team:

"They deserve the credit. The credit belongs to the players. I can't identify anything in my own work that has been the key to… to making them do this. I simply do my normal job, and they're responding individually and as a team… they're responding in a… spectacular way.

There's been tremendous progress, although I think the fact that we had so much possession today and… and… therefore had very little defensive work to do also helped. But we should also point out that whenever we lose the ball, our reaction has always been excellent.

As for what you mentioned, there's an image in front of my dugout in the second half when we lose the ball, Arda is out of position and Kylian makes… a sprint to get back and close down the right-hand side of the block. I think that's a good example. But it's only one example. They're very supportive of one another and very united. And as I said to Real Madrid TV, in my experience, this team smells good."

It was quite a heated game, but not anything the Real Madrid coach was not expecting from a stadium like Mestalla:

"Look, Mestalla is… Mestalla is passion. Throughout history, Valencia has always been… a difficult stadium. A stadium that demands a lot from its teams and players. When they're playing against a Real Madrid side that is individually and collectively far superior, I think… the frustration increases.

And… it pushes the players towards a style of play that allows them to compete for the result. The good thing for us is that we remained very calm and… didn't react. And so on. The red-card incident looked very clear to me from a distance.

As for the yellow card for Kylian… I don't know. I don't know. I know it was potentially a goal, potentially a goalscoring opportunity. I don't know whether the referee could or couldn't have allowed play to continue, but, to be honest, I thought… I could be wrong, I don't know, but from the dugout it looked to me as though the referee had an outstanding game. An outstanding game.

Obviously, this was a stadium where… where people complain. The Bernabéu is one thing, where people go to watch the match calmly, whereas Santander and Valencia are different… These are stadiums where people want to be part of the game. And when they're frustrated with the result, they complain a little more and create a little more atmosphere. But it was all within the bounds of normality."

While being worried about the upcoming international break, Mourinho did not want to ask anything from his players' national sides:

"No, no. I'm not going to speak to anyone because… I don't know whether I'll ever become a national-team coach one day. I don't know. But I have a feeling that if I ever do, I'll be very demanding… I'll be very demanding with the clubs. I'll think about myself and my team; that's how I see it.

That's why I don't feel I can call anyone, even if it's my friend Carlo… But in Carlo's case, look carefully: the players going with him are Vinicius, who should play, and… Endrick, who I would be grateful to see Carlo give some playing time to. So… Carlo isn't the one I'm worried about.

But I also don't think national-team coaches want a player to get injured through accumulated fatigue. I think they also owe it to the players to act professionally when it comes to their recovery. Let's hope… let's hope we're lucky."

The Portuguese coach once again expressed his concern with players' fatigue:

"As I was saying… My only concern is this accumulation of fatigue. They're obviously extremely fatigued. They're extremely fatigued. They have to join their national teams on Monday… and on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday they'll still be getting rid of the muscle fatigue they're carrying. I'm not talking about mental fatigue, because when you're winning, you don't suffer from mental fatigue. But physical fatigue, yes. They're… they're… But, as I said, I respect the national-team coaches."

The team's form has improved lately, but the Real Madrid coach assured that his team remained composed even when they were not getting the expected results:

"No, what makes me happy is precisely the fact that… using the word you used, 'chaos', after we lost that match… We were never in chaos. We always remained calm. We understood why we had lost that match. We understood where we could improve. We always had… a great deal of… a great deal of composure.

I'll always fight to ensure that people remain balanced during the good times. I always tell them that winning matches at a club like Real Madrid… you can't fall into… into a state of uncontrollable joy. Winning matches at Real Madrid has to be normal.

I see a… a happy dressing room, with horrible music playing loudly; absolutely horrible… But the people are calm, because the message is that winning matches should be normal. When we lose, that's when we enter your 'chaos'. And that can then spread into the 'chaos' of… the wider Madrid environment and its supporters. But in here, we're calm, we're calm."

While revealing that he is suffering from a fever, Mourinho also revealed what he told the Valencia coach after the game:

"Tomorrow, I'll go to the NFL if my temperature drops from 40 to 39 degrees, because I'm dying. I'm dying. I'm tired, I have a fever. I'm dying. But if I recover, I'll go.

And what was your other question? Ah, no, no! I left immediately, with my friend Aguirre… and it was a pleasure to tell him what I said after the match: 'Don't be sad, because my players are much better than yours.' And it's true. The problem isn't Aguirre, who is a great coach with a wealth of experience. But the truth is that Real Madrid's players… are very good. And coaches who have players like mine… are closer to winning."

With this win, Real Madrid can go into the November international break with much more ease of mind than they enjoyed going into the September international break. Hopefully, there would be no undesirable surprises for them during the break, and all of their players will be able to return healthy to their team in two weeks' time.

articles.title: Report: Money too good to turn down for Bayern Munich for January friendly vs. Ajax in Kenya
articles.summary: Money was the main motivator here.
articles.body:
The presence of a winter break in German football gives Bundesliga players a chance to spend around a week and a half with their families and recuperate while multiple other leagues play through Christmas and beyond. When the players return from their vacation, however, regaining match fitness is crucial ahead of the league's restart. Given the relatively short timeframe, Bayern Munich has always preferred to limit themselves to just one friendly and keep it close to home, as evidenced by multiple recent January friendlies against RB Salzburg.

This season, however, the plan is different. Bayern will travel to Nairobi, Kenya, to play a friendly against Ajax Amsterdam.According to reporter Manuel Bonke, (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) the friendly was not scheduled for the sake of preparing for the upcoming Bundesliga restart, but because the money was simply too good to turn down:

Bayern will receive €5m for the trip to Nairobi, Kenya to play a friendly against Ajax on January 5th. Vincent Kompany approved the trip, which was then handled by Marketing and sales director Rouven Kasper. 'For that kind of money, you have to do it', it was said at Säbener Straße.

It certainly is an unprecedented amount of money, though it is worth wondering how it will affect the Bavarians' return to the Bundesliga season. They will face Borussia Mönchengladbach on January 9th, meaning the players will need to fly all the way back to Munich and get just over three days to rest before their next match. Will this be the only friendly of the winter pre-season camp? These are not insurmountable issues, and it is good that Kompany had the option to veto the trip. Furthermore, it should be nice for the fans in Kenya to see Bayern play Ajax. On a side note, it has also been far too long since Bayern has faced Ajax, but one can wonder how such a trip will affect Bayern's season restart.

Ultimately, though, money makes the world go round—and that is a lot of money for one friendly.

articles.title: Jon Sumrall admits Florida Gators’ offense feels ‘a little bit lost’ after thrashing by Oklahoma
articles.summary: Jon Sumrall cited a lack of identity on the field that hindered the Florida Gators in their 23-7 loss to the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday afternoon. Sumrall...
articles.body:
Jon Sumrall cited a lack of identity on the field that hindered the Florida Gators in their 23-7 loss to the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday afternoon.

Sumrall is going through his first year as the Gators' head coach. He is coming off an incredible stint with the Tulane Green Wave, having led them to the College Football Playoffs in 2025.

Despite a great 4-0 start to the season, Florida has since regressed throughout SEC action. They have lost four of their last five games, suffering another disappointing display on the offensive side of the ball. Sumrall reflected on the loss after the game, believing that the identity hasn't been the same as it was to begin the campaign.

"I think early in the year, there were some things that you could see were our identity. Right now, we feel a little bit lost, and I don't really know that I can pinpoint what I know that we're good at day in day out. There's going to be tough games, but you have to be able to know, hey, this is what we're good at, and this is how we're going to hang in the game. And right now, we don't have that identity clear enough offensively, which is frustrating," Sumrall said, per reporter Chandler Dantzler.

How Jon Sumrall, Florida performed against Oklahoma

Jon Sumrall and the Florida Gators need one more win to secure bowl eligibility. However, it won't be this weekend as they couldn't keep up with Oklahoma at home.

Oklahoma controlled the game from start to finish. They did an excellent job containing Florida's attack, only conceding a touchdown in the second quarter.

Trammell Jones had a brutal day leading the offense. He only completed 10 out of 22 passes for 133 yards and two interceptions. Jadan Baugh led rushers with eight carries for 35 yards and a touchdown, while Duke Clark caught four passes for 70 yards.

The Gators will look to bounce back in their next matchup, being on the road. They take on the Kentucky Wildcats in Week 11 as kickoff commences on Nov. 14.

articles.title: Michael Carrick, Sir Alex Ferguson and Man United’s seemingly impossible question
articles.summary: As the club celebrate the 40th anniversary since the great Scot arrived at Old Trafford from Aberdeen, it is the task of following in Sir Alex’s footsteps th...
articles.body:
Even as he risks being consigned to Manchester United history, Michael Carrick was talking about Manchester United's history. They are celebrating one of their managers and, whether or not Aston Villa are defeated on Sunday, it is not him. Friday marked the 40th anniversary of Sir Alex Ferguson 's appointment. There is a dinner this weekend to honour the great Scot.

There is also the chance Sunday marks Carrick's last game at the helm. Ferguson has been in charge for two-thirds of the last four decades and end his tenure of his own volition, retiring after 26-and-a-half years. Carrick could become the seventh man sacked since then , without even including the interim appointment Ralf Rangnick. He is already the fifth of Ferguson's former players to have served as caretaker manager.

Ferguson has been the inspiration for them all. He remains the benchmark, the gold standard, but also the anomaly. A banner at Old Trafford, commemorating Ferguson, reads: "The impossible dream". For much of the last 13 years, following him has seemed similarly impossible.

"Well, it's not impossible," Carrick countered. "Anything's possible. You've got to build, you've got to be realistic. You've got to put things in perspective as well, the recent history that we've had and where we want to get to, but it's not going to happen in a blink of an eye. It's not going to happen overnight. Success does take time, and we don't like having to spend time, but it does take a period of time to build."

That is true. That said, the inconvenient details are that it seemed to happen overnight when Carrick had an immediate impact upon his return to Old Trafford in January and that results show regression this season.

United enter the weekend in 17th place in the Premier League , in a 14th consecutive campaign without a title challenge. In all competitions, they have a lone win in their last 10 matches. Matheus Cunha's dramatic decider against Roma on Tuesday prompted suggestions it was Carrick's Mark Robins moment ; there is a parallel of sorts because, a couple of weeks after Robins scored against Nottingham Forest in January 1990, Ferguson's United were 17th.

Then he was more than three years into his reign. Now Carrick is only three months into his first season after being appointed. If several of his predecessors think there was a brutality to their sacking, others can feel the United powerbrokers afforded them too much time. But the broader trend is that managers tend to be afforded less time now.

"The game's certainly changed, no doubt," Carrick reflected. "It always does. It evolved, and it had evolved to the stage probably after Sir Matt [Busby] in the years after that, to then Sir Alex."

The mention of Busby underlines the heights United have touched under two great empire-builders of managers, but rarely under anyone else. Busby took up the job in 1945 so only one managerial appointment United have made in the last eight decades, and only two in the last 12, have been definitively superb; a handful of others, whether Tommy Doherty, Ron Atkinson or Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, may be termed qualified successes, but no more. Should Carrick go with United in the lower reaches of the table, he would not even belong in that bracket.

But the past is United's constant companion. "There's always different things to compare, but always we've got to live in the present as well," said Carrick; it is worth noting he is less openly nostalgic than his friend Solskjaer but it is evident neither had the track record to manage United. Their playing days were a factor.

There is forever the hope Ferguson's magic has rubbed off on someone, anyone. Carrick is a very different character to his former manager: less fiery, less cutting in his comments, less of a dictator and more of a diplomat.

But as a midfielder, he was a favourite of Ferguson's. "I'm probably closer to him now and speak more to him now than I did when I was playing," Carrick said. "I think the relationships change over time and that's only natural. Ever since I came here, the impact he had on me as an individual was immense. Not necessarily directly as in talking all the time and advice all the time. Personally, it was more of the influence that he had and the habits that you try and pick up from him, as did everyone around the football club over that period of time. Then you move on and evolve a little bit into a friendship, really, which is really nice."

His friend casts a long shadow. Carrick won five Premier Leagues and appeared in three Champions League finals, all under Ferguson, though he played on under David Moyes, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho. The 84-year-old collected silverware in a way that others of his generation collected stamps. He made it appear natural.

"There's a lot of winning, a lot of trophies and a lot of success," said Carrick. "It's difficult to bring success. It was difficult then. It's difficult now. It just shows you how tough it is to have sustained success. Again, we've got to live in the moment." But the moment is troubled and United can forever live in the past. As the celebrations of Ferguson show, it is often a preferable place.

articles.title: Real Madrid legend Marcelo mocks Valencia defender after heated Mestalla encounter
articles.summary: Real Madrid continued their impressive run of form with a convincing 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla.It was the eighth consecutive victory for Jose Mou...
articles.body:
Real Madrid continued their impressive run of form with a convincing 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla .

It was the eighth consecutive victory for Jose Mourinho's side across all competitions, as Los Blancos head into the November international break in strong form.

The encounter against Valencia was not without controversy, though, with defender Pablo Maffeo involved.

The defender, who has a history of heated encounters with Los Blancos , once again found himself at the centre of attention.

This time, however, former Real Madrid superstar Marcelo could not resist taking a dig at the Spaniard on social media.

"Maffeo really has it in for MADRID… my goodness," Marcelo wrote on X , mockingly referring to the Valencia defender as 'Masfeo'.

"And a goal," the Brazilian added, celebrating Madrid's breakthrough during the first half.

The incident came after Maffeo was penalised for a foul on Kylian Mbappe just outside Valencia's penalty area.

Maffeo received a yellow card for the challenge. Mbappe's resulting free-kick struck the wall, and Fede Valverde collected the rebound to score Real Madrid's opening goal.

Maffeo was visibly frustrated with the decision and subsequently criticised the refereeing during his half-time interview with DAZN.

"I don't feel like doing this interview at all. It's rubbish," he complained , before insisting that the foul leading to Madrid's opening goal should never have been awarded.

Maffeo has been involved in a series of controversies against Real Madrid, dating back to his time at Mallorca.

At his former club, he was often involved in heated exchanges with Vinicius Jr., including controversial challenges and gestures towards the Brazilian.

Pablo Maffeo's personal vendetta against Real Madrid are well documented. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

Although Maffeo previously claimed the pair had resolved their differences, it looks like he has now found a new bone to pick with Real Madrid.

The important thing for Mourinho's men was that they had the last laugh on Saturday and secured all three points.

Maffeo is likely to receive a hostile reception when he visits the Santiago Bernabeu , and it remains to be seen how this battle pans out in future meetings.

articles.title: 🎥 May they live forever: Carlos Espí reunites with his grans at Mestalla 🥹
