articles.body:
Real Madrid came out on top in an intense league clash against Valencia at Mestalla. However, the match's most touching moment came just after the referee blew the final whistle. Carlos Espí took center stage after the game as he headed straight toward one of the lower sections of the stands.

His two grandmothers were waiting there, visibly moved after watching the academy graduate make his debut and give his all against one of the toughest opponents in the league.

The footballer shared a long, heartfelt embrace with both women, creating a moment of genuine affection and gratitude that soon drew applause from nearby fans.

Television cameras captured the tender scene, revealing the more human side of professional football, away from the competitive tension and the final score.

This is not the first time Carlos Espí's grandmothers have been in the spotlight. They were also present when the player from Tavernes was unveiled as a new member of Real Madrid's squad. An iconic image with the Champions League trophies behind them got everyone talking.

articles.title: Roma sensation Rodrigo Mora opens up on Portugal's first squad without Cristiano Ronaldo after incredible scoring streak
articles.summary: Rodrigo Mora has enjoyed a spectacular rise at Roma, cementing his place in the starting XI with a clinical run of goals that has earned him international re...
articles.body:
Rodrigo Mora has enjoyed a spectacular rise at Roma, cementing his place in the starting XI with a clinical run of goals that has earned him international recognition. The young forward is now set to join the Portugal national team for their first fixtures since the departure of a legendary figure.

The dawn of a new era has arrived for the Selecao, and Mora finds himself at the heart of it. Following Ronaldo's decision to step away from international football , the Roma trequartista has been identified as one of the key figures to lead the line. The transition comes at a pivotal moment, with the national team naming its first roster since the veteran attacker brought his storied career to a close after a reported disagreement with the coaching staff.

"I'm proud, it's a pleasure to play for the national team. Ronaldo won't be there, but he's my idol; I learned a lot from him when we shared a dressing room," Mora told Sky Sport Italia when asked about the vacuum left by the former Real Madrid man, as quoted by Forza Roma .

Mora is currently enjoying the most productive spell of his career, having found the net in three consecutive league matches for Roma. His latest contribution proved vital in a hard-fought victory against Sassuolo , further cementing his place in the starting eleven. The youngster was quick to credit his teammates for his recent surge in front of goal.

"A great passage from Malen, I tried and today I was lucky to score another important goal and Roma continues to win," the forward said. Mora also touched upon his increased involvement in the squad compared to the opening weeks of the season, showing a mature perspective on the rotations of professional football. "Football is crazy, sometimes you play and sometimes you don't but you have to be ready," he added.

Building chemistry with Soulé and Dybala

Part of Mora's success in the capital has been his burgeoning relationship with fellow attackers Matias Soule and Paulo Dybala. The trio has quickly become one of the most exciting creative units in Serie A. Mora admitted that he is still learning how to best compliment his teammates, but he feels the understanding on the pitch is improving with every passing fixture. "Playing with Mati is beautiful, everything becomes easier. Then it's fantastic, he helped me a lot. Paulo... no adjectives are needed, he is very strong: I am happy to play with them," Mora noted.

He credited the demanding nature of Gasperini's coaching for his overall development, particularly his improvements in the defensive phase, which he believes were decisive in earning his latest international call-up. "The coach is very demanding, even defensively. I'm improving in everything, every day. This work was crucial for the call-up: it's a great moment for me and my family," he stated.

Looking back at his journey, Mora seems almost surprised by how quickly he has adapted to the pressures of top-flight Italian football. Having moved from Porto, he remains deeply grateful to his former club for providing the foundation of his career. He noted that while there are always highs and lows in football, maintaining balance and following the manager's instructions has been key to his consistency.

"It's not easy... Looking back, I'm in my third professional career: I didn't expect such a rapid rise. I'm grateful to Porto; I owe them everything. To my younger self, I'd say he's working well; I'm grateful for the man I am today," he reflected.

articles.title: García Plaza no se rinde con Vargas
articles.standfirst: El extremo recibió los pitos del Sánchez-Pizjuán
articles.summary: El extremo recibió los pitos del Sánchez-Pizjuán
articles.body: Llega el parón de noviembre y con él, el éxodo de jugadores que deberán cumplir con los diferentes compromisos internacionales de sus selecciones. Uno de ellos, en el caso del Sevilla, es Rubén Vargas. Aunque el extremo no termina de arrancar, Murat Yakin no ha dudado en citarle para los partidos que Suiza disputará frente a Eslovenia y ante Escocia, en el que coincidirá con Robbie Ure, compañero de filas en Nervión. A Vargas le puede venir bien el cambio de aires y su paso por la helvética para recuperar sensaciones y resetear tras la última cita liguera con el Alavés. El '11' blanquirrojo fue titular, falló un penalti, dejó detalles de calidad, aunque insuficientes, y fue despedido con pitos por la grada del Sánchez-Pizjuán. Hace justo un año, el extremo marcó un penalti que fue decisivo para derrotar a Osasuna en el estadio nervionense justo antes de un parón. Juanlu provocó la pena máxima en un choque con Moi Gómez que serviría al Sevilla para sumar tres puntos de oro y para desactivar el botón del pánico después de tres derrotas consecutivas frente a Mallorca, Real Sociedad y Atlético de Madrid. Desde entonces no ha vuelto a ser el mismo. Las lesiones lastraron su recuperación y su continuidad en el césped. Después, su buen papel en el Mundial el pasado verano con Suiza hizo soñar a los aficionados con un regreso estelar o con una venta millonaria que ayudase a apuntalar la plantilla. Pero nada de eso ha sucedido. "Aquí ha lanzado penaltis en el Sevilla, los ha marcado, por lo que no es cosa nueva”, decía García Plaza en defensa de su jugador tras el partido frente al Alavés. El técnico necesita su mejor versión. El derbi frente al Betis, el primero del curso, espera a la vuelta de la esquina.

articles.title: Real Madrid rediscover collective identity under Mourinho with eight consecutive victories
articles.summary: Real Madrid have undergone a remarkable transformation over the past month, and the results have been there for everyone to see.Los Blancos secured a 3-0 vic...
articles.body:
Real Madrid have undergone a remarkable transformation over the past month, and the results have been there for everyone to see.

Los Blancos secured a 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla last night to make it eight wins in their last eight games.

Jose Mourinho's tactical modifications have worked wonders for the Spanish club, and the performances have also improved.

According to MARCA , he has moulded the team into a more cohesive and disciplined unit after a difficult start to his second spell in the Spanish capital.

Mourinho's Real Madrid growing stronger collectively

Madrid have scored 24 goals across those eight matches, averaging three per game, while keeping three clean sheets.

The winning run includes victories over Barcelona in El Clasico and Roma, RB Leipzig and AEK Athens in the Champions League.

Saturday's 3-0 victory over Valencia offered another example of their progress, with the team breaking down a resolute defensive unit.

Jose Mourinho has galvanized the team at Real Madrid. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Los Che actually started the game very well, causing problems for Madrid, but goals from Fede Valverde, Arda Guler and Kylian Mbappe helped Mourinho's men secure the three points.

The most encouraging aspect of Real Madrid's evolution is that the team no longer seem excessively dependent on individual brilliance.

Mbappe, Guler, Diomande and Bellingham have come together to form an excellent attacking quartet, and their strengths complement each other perfectly.

Mourinho's defensive demands making the difference

There was one moment in the Valencia game that perfectly summed up the defensive transformation under Mourinho.

When Guler was caught out of position after Madrid lost possession, Mbappe sprinted across to cover the exposed space and restore the team's defensive shape.

One of the biggest criticisms levelled at the Frenchman was that he was not contributing enough defensively.

How will Mourinho integrate Vinicius into the team? (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images)

That has changed now, with everyone willing to put the team ahead of themselves. Mourinho will love the fact that his side have almost reached that stage.

It remains to be seen how the dynamics change once Vinicius Jr. returns from suspension and how the manager reintegrates him.

If the team can find a way for Vinicius to thrive within this system too, they could become even more devastating in the coming months. It remains to be seen how Mourinho handles his return.

articles.title: Women's Rugby League World Cup: Australia set up fifth straight final vs New Zealand after scare vs debutants Fiji
articles.summary: Abbi Church scores four tries as Jillaroos come from behind to win 30-14 and reach next weekend's final in Brisbane; Fiji can take plenty of pride from performances in first World Cup; Australia have won last three tournaments; New Zealand blanked Samoa 32-0 in Saturday's first semi-final
articles.body:
The Jillaroos, who have beaten New Zealand in the last three finals since they were thumped 34-0 by the the Kiwi Ferns in the 2008 showpiece in Brisbane, won 30-14 against Fiji as Abbi Church notched four tries.

Fiji opened up a shock 8-0 lead as Luisa Yaranamua followed a penalty by scoring a try that she also converted, leaving the home side trailing for the first time in the tournament, but Australia made it 8-8 by the break and then dominated the second half.

Australia had won all three of their group games, scoring 242 points and conceding just six, but this was a real test.

Church leapt over the line for the hosts' first try after 25 minutes before Tamika Upton doubled that tally four minutes later to level the scores.

The Jillaroos failed to add the bonus points for both tries, though, as Jocelyn Kelleher missed the conversions.

Fiji ended the first half well, although Australia then took over in the second period as Church scored again prior to a Jaime Chapman try - Kelleher applying the conversions this time.

Church then completed her hat-trick after catching Tarryn Aiken's kick and grounding the ball.

A converted effort from Maria Paseka gave Fiji hope but Church had the final say with her fourth try of the evening - jinking away from two defenders around 30 metres out before sprinting clear to score.

A Fiji team with nowhere near the level of experience of their opponents can be proud of their performance in this game and the tournament as a whole, with the World Cup novices recording group-stage wins over Papua New Guinea and France and pushing New Zealand in an 18-12 defeat in their other match.

New Zealand, aiming to deny Australia a fourth straight World Cup title in Brisbane next Sunday, defeated Samoa 32-0 in Saturday's first semi-final in Newcastle.

articles.body:
Tries: Church 4, Upton, Chapman Goals: Kelleher 3

Tries: Yaranamua, Paseka Goals: Yaranamua 3

Australia have reached their fifth successive Women's Rugby League World Cup final as they seek a fourth consecutive title - but they were made to work harder than anyone expected.

They had breezed through the group stages and there looked to be little to stop the procession.

But World Cup debutants Fiji had other ideas. For 40 minutes, one of the biggest surprises in the history of rugby league looked eminently possible.

Order was eventually restored, thanks largely to four tries from Abbi Church, which set Australia on their way to a 30-14 victory.

They will face old rivals New Zealand in the final next Sunday in Brisbane, kicking off at 05:10 GMT.

But having given New Zealand a scare in their opening match before losing 18-12, Fiji came out at Sydney Football Stadium fully intent to unsettle and confront the red-hot tournament favourites.

In doing so, they became the first side since New Zealand in the 2013 World Cup final to open the scoring in a game against Australia, who trailed for the first time at this tournament.

The tournament debutants put pressure on the Australia line from the start. Soon the entire Aussie team caught the bug with simple drops and brainless errors, and after 12 minutes Simaima Taufa conceded a penalty under the posts.

Fiji opted to kick for two points. Four minutes later, they went all the way.

Captain Sereana Naitokatoka stole the ball from Jaime Chapman 10 metres from the Australia line, and they drove through the defence for half-back Luisa Yaranamua to score. She also converted to give Fiji an astonishing 8-0 lead.

At last Australia sparked into life, and two tries in the final 10 minutes of the opening half brought them level.

Church drove over in the right corner, before Tamika Upton slipped through the defence as Australia returned pressure following a Fiji drop-out.

But Jocelyn Kelleher missed twice from the tee to allow Fiji in at half-time level. Had Upton not brilliantly tipped a Fiji grubber behind, Australia would have trailed.

Whatever coach Jess Skinner said in the changing room woke Australia up, and they took control.

Church completed her treble - the third a brilliant catch from a booming Tarryn Aiken kick to the corner and before grounding the ball at full tilt - either side of Chapman diving over.

Normal service resumed. But at last, the Jillaroos have been proved fallible - with a late Maria Paseka try providing a deserved flourish for fearless Fiji.

Church, though, had the last word for Australia - collecting Losana Lutu's kick around 30 metres from her own line before racing clear to score.
